# Restrict Models and Providers
Source: https://ngrok.com/docs/ai-gateway/examples/model-filtering

These examples show how to limit which providers and models an ngrok.ai access key can call, using JSON or the dashboard.

Use an [access key configuration](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations) to restrict providers and models. Requests outside the allowlist are rejected before they reach an upstream provider.

## Allow specific providers

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "name": "OpenAI only",
  "access": {
    "providers": { "allow": ["openai"] }
  },
  "router": {
    "rules": [
      { "provider": "openai", "steps": [{ "type": "ngrok" }] }
    ]
  }
}
```

Assign this configuration to an access key. That key can only reach OpenAI models.

## Allow specific models

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "name": "Cheap models only",
  "access": {
    "models": {
      "allow": ["openai/gpt-4o-mini", "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5"]
    }
  }
}
```

Model IDs use the catalog form `author/model`, as shown in the [model catalog](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/model-catalog). This form matches the model on every provider that serves it. To pin a provider, prefix it: `openai:openai/gpt-4o`. See [Restrict providers and models](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/restrict-providers-and-models#allow-specific-models).

## Block pass-through models

If clients use provider prefixes for uncatalogued models, include only known model IDs in the allowlist. Requests for models not listed are rejected.

## Via dashboard

Follow [Create a configuration](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations#create-a-configuration) in [app.ngrok.ai](https://app.ngrok.ai) to set allowed providers and models, then assign the configuration to your access keys.

# Multi-Key Failover
Source: https://ngrok.com/docs/ai-gateway/examples/multi-key-failover

This example shows how backup provider keys keep your requests working when one of your keys is rate limited or stops working.

Add multiple provider keys to the same routing rule in an [access key configuration](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations). The gateway tries keys in order when one hits a rate limit or an auth error.

Your application sends only an [access key](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/access-keys)—provider keys are stored in app.ngrok.ai and referenced by the configuration.

## Setup

1. [Add two or more provider keys](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys#add-a-provider-key) for the same provider
2. Create or edit a configuration with an ordered `user` step listing both key IDs
3. Assign the configuration to your access key

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "router": {
    "rules": [
      {
        "provider": "openai",
        "steps": [
          {
            "type": "user",
            "keySelectionStrategy": "ordered",
            "keys": [
              { "id": "aigpk_primary" },
              { "id": "aigpk_backup" }
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Failover sequence

```
1. Request arrives with access key
2. Try primary OpenAI key → Rate limited (429)
3. Try backup OpenAI key → Success
```

* [Multi-provider failover](/docs/ai-gateway/examples/multi-provider-failover): Fail over across providers


# Multi-Provider Failover
Source: https://ngrok.com/docs/ai-gateway/examples/multi-provider-failover

These examples show how to keep your app working during a provider outage by giving ngrok.ai a list of models to try in order.

You can configure fail over by listing multiple models in a request. The gateway tries each model in order until one succeeds. Combine this with an [access key configuration](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations) that allows the providers you need.

Your app sends an [access key](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/access-keys); the AI Gateway routes to each provider with the credentials from your configuration.

## Basic example

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1",
    api_key="ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx",
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-4o",
    extra_body={
        "models": ["anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6"],
    },
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}],
)
```

Or in raw JSON:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "model": "gpt-4o",
  "models": ["anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6"],
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
}
```

## How it works

1. Request arrives with your access key
2. Gateway tries `gpt-4o` (OpenAI)
3. On failure, tries `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`
4. Returns the first successful response

Both providers must be allowed by the access key's configuration, with routing rules that supply credentials (pay with credits or provider keys).

## Configuration example

Allow OpenAI and Anthropic on one key:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "name": "Multi-provider production",
  "access": {
    "providers": { "allow": ["openai", "anthropic"] }
  },
  "router": {
    "rules": [
      { "provider": "openai", "steps": [{ "type": "ngrok" }] },
      { "provider": "anthropic", "steps": [{ "type": "ngrok" }] }
    ]
  }
}
```

Use provider keys instead of `ngrok` steps when billing should go to your provider accounts.

# AI Gateway FAQ
Source: https://ngrok.com/docs/ai-gateway/faq

Find quick answers to common ngrok.ai questions, from setting up access keys and buying credits to troubleshooting failed requests.

***

## Getting started

### What URL do I send requests to?

Send model requests to `https://gateway.ngrok.ai`.

If you're using an OpenAI-compatible SDK, set the base URL to:

```text theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1
```

For example:

```typescript theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
import OpenAI from "openai";

const client = new OpenAI({
  baseURL: "https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1",
  apiKey: "ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx"
});
```

See the [Quickstart](/docs/ai-gateway/quickstart) for a full example.

### Can I use my existing OpenAI SDK?

Yes.
The AI Gateway supports OpenAI-compatible requests, so you can usually keep your SDK and change the base URL and API key.

Use your ngrok.ai access key as the API key, and set the base URL to `https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1`.

See [SDK Integration](/docs/ai-gateway/sdks) for examples.

### Do I need a provider account to use ngrok.ai?

Not always.

For many providers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and DeepSeek, you can skip adding your own provider key and pay with credits instead.

For other built-in providers, or if you want usage billed to your own provider account, you can add a provider key.

### Do I need credits?

Yes.
Every request through ngrok.ai requires credits for the gateway processing fee.

If ngrok.ai supplies the upstream provider credentials, credits also pay the upstream model cost.
If you bring your own provider key, the provider bills you for model usage and credits only pay the gateway processing fee.

See [Credits](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/credits).

### Do I need an ngrok subscription plan?

No, not to use the AI Gateway itself.
You can sign in at [app.ngrok.ai](https://app.ngrok.ai), purchase AI Gateway credits, create an access key, and send requests to `https://gateway.ngrok.ai`.

You may need an ngrok platform plan for platform features on the same account, such as team members or internal endpoints for custom providers.
Manage those features from [dashboard.ngrok.com](https://dashboard.ngrok.com).

See [Credits](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/credits).

### Can my team sign in with SSO?

Yes.
app.ngrok.ai uses your ngrok account to sign in, so it uses your account's single sign-on (SAML or OpenID Connect, with providers like Okta).

SSO requires the Pay-as-you-go plan with the SSO & RBAC add-on.
Set it up on your [ngrok account settings](https://dashboard.ngrok.com/settings).
See [dashboard single sign-on](/docs/iam/sso).

Role-based permissions inside app.ngrok.ai aren't available yet.

## Keys and credentials

### Which key do I put in my app?

Use an access key.

Your app sends the access key to `https://gateway.ngrok.ai`.
Don't put provider keys, ngrok API keys, or AI Gateway API keys in your app's model requests.

See [Access keys](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/access-keys).

### What is the difference between access keys, provider keys, AI Gateway API keys, and ngrok API keys?

| Key | Used for |
| - | - |
| Access key | Authenticates model requests to `gateway.ngrok.ai` |
| Provider key | Authenticates ngrok.ai to an upstream provider |
| AI Gateway API key | Automates AI Gateway resources through `api.ngrok.ai` |
| ngrok API key | Manages ngrok platform resources through `api.ngrok.com` |

Most applications only need an access key in runtime code.

### What are access keys?

Access keys are what your app uses to authenticate model requests to `https://gateway.ngrok.ai`.

It’s a good idea to create separate access keys for different applications, environments, or teams so you can easily track usage, control access, and revoke keys if needed.

### Can I create multiple access keys?

Yes, you can.
It’s a good idea to create separate access keys for each app, environment, client, or team.

Doing this makes it easier to track usage, revoke access when needed, and apply different access key configurations.

### What happens if I lose an access key?

Access key tokens are only shown once when they're created.

If you lose one, delete the old access key, create a new one, and update your application with the new token.

### Are access keys scoped to endpoints?

No.
Access keys are account-scoped and work with `https://gateway.ngrok.ai`.

You don't need to create or manage a custom endpoint URL to use the AI Gateway.

### Can I use different keys for different teams?

Yes.
Create separate access keys for each team or client.

To control what each key can call, assign different [access key configurations](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations).
Configurations can limit providers, models, and routing credentials.

### Do I need provider keys?

It depends on the provider and how you want billing to work.

For models you can [pay for with credits](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/model-catalog#billing-and-provider-credentials), you don't need to add your own provider key.
That includes models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, xAI, Moonshot AI, Z.ai, and others.

For other built-in providers, or if you want upstream usage billed to your own provider account, add a [provider key](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys).

### Can I bring my own key for every provider?

Yes.
Every built-in provider accepts your own provider key, including OpenAI and Anthropic.

ngrok-managed keys, where you pay with ngrok.ai credits instead of a provider account, are available for supported models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, xAI, Moonshot AI, Z.ai, and others.
The [model catalog](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/model-catalog#billing-and-provider-credentials) shows which providers need your own key.

Add provider keys on the [Providers page](https://app.ngrok.ai/providers) in app.ngrok.ai or with the [Provider Keys API](/docs/ai-gateway/api-reference/provider-keys/create).
See [Bring your own provider key](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys).

### Are provider keys exposed to my app?

No.
Your app sends an access key to the AI Gateway.

Provider keys are stored in app.ngrok.ai and used server-side when ngrok.ai calls the upstream provider.
They don't need to be stored in your application code.

### Does ngrok.ai provide provider API keys?

No.
ngrok.ai doesn't give you provider API keys to copy or use outside the gateway.

For models you can pay for with credits, ngrok.ai supplies the provider credentials.
For other providers, or when you want to use your own provider account, add your own provider key.

### How do I rotate keys?

For access keys, create a new access key, update your application, then delete the old access key.

For provider keys, rotate the stored provider key value so configurations that reference the key can keep using the same key ID.
See [Bring your own provider key](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys#rotating-provider-keys).

### Can I manage the AI Gateway with an API?

Yes.
The AI Gateway API at `https://api.ngrok.ai` manages access keys, access key configurations, providers, provider keys, gateway settings, credits, models, and usage.

Authenticate with an AI Gateway API key, which you create on the [Settings](https://app.ngrok.ai/settings) page.

The full [OpenAPI spec](https://api.ngrok.ai/openapi.yaml) is public, so you can generate a client in any language.

See the [AI Gateway API reference](/docs/ai-gateway/api-reference/overview).

## Credits and billing

### What do credits pay for?

Credits always pay the AI Gateway processing fee.

When you pay with credits, credits also pay the provider's model cost.
If you bring your own provider key, the provider bills you for model usage and credits only pay the gateway processing fee.

### How much is the processing fee?

The ngrok.ai processing fee is `$0.05` per million tokens.

### Do credits expire?

Yes.
Credits expire 365 days after purchase.

### What happens when credits run out?

The gateway rejects new requests with HTTP 402 and `ERR_NGROK_27206` until you purchase more credits from the [Billing page](https://app.ngrok.ai/billing).
That's true even if you use your own provider keys, since every request pays a small processing fee from your credits.

To avoid this, turn on [automatic top-up](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/credits#automatic-top-up) so your balance refills before it runs out.

### What's the minimum credit purchase?

The minimum credit purchase is `$5.00`.

You can purchase credits from the [Billing page](https://app.ngrok.ai/billing).
Your balance can't go above `$500.00`.

### Can credits top up automatically?

Yes.
Turn on automatic top-up on the [Billing page](https://app.ngrok.ai/billing).
When your balance falls to an amount you choose, ngrok.ai charges your saved card and tops it back up.
You can also set a maximum to spend each billing period.
See [Automatic top-up](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/credits#automatic-top-up).

### Are AI Gateway credits the same as ngrok platform billing?

No.
You purchase and use AI Gateway credits in [app.ngrok.ai](https://app.ngrok.ai).

ngrok platform billing for products managed through [dashboard.ngrok.com](https://dashboard.ngrok.com) is separate, and certain features such as team members and internal endpoints for self-hosted models require an ngrok subscription.

## Models and providers

### Which providers are supported?

The AI Gateway includes built-in support for:

* OpenAI
* Anthropic
* Google
* DeepSeek
* xAI
* Groq
* Mistral AI
* Amazon Bedrock
* Moonshot AI
* Z.ai
* QwenCloud
* MiniMax
* Tencent TokenHub
* Typesafe AI
* Liquid AI
* LLM API
* Morph
* Novita AI
* OpenRouter
* Hyperbolic
* InceptionLabs
* Inference.net

You can also connect self-hosted or private OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-compatible endpoints, such as Ollama, vLLM, or Azure OpenAI, as [custom providers](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/custom-providers).

See the [Model Catalog](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/model-catalog) for the full list.

### Which providers can I call without adding a provider key?

You can see which providers require a provider key in the Model Catalog by checking the **needs provider keys** column.

Other built-in providers require you to add your own provider key before sending traffic.

### How do I choose a model?

Set the `model` field in your request.

Use a model ID when you want ngrok.ai to resolve the provider:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "model": "gpt-4o",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
}
```

Use `provider:model` when you want to choose the provider explicitly:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "model": "openai:gpt-4o",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
}
```

See [Choose a model](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/model-selection-strategies).

### How do I know which models are available?

Built-in providers and models are listed in the [Model Catalog](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/model-catalog).

The catalog includes provider IDs, model IDs, context windows, output token limits, modalities, and provider key requirements.

Custom providers declare their own models when you create them.

### Can clients use models not in the catalog?

Yes, if the request uses a provider-qualified model name and the provider allows pass-through for that model.

For example:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "model": "openai:gpt-5-preview",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
}
```

To restrict an access key to approved models only, configure a model allowlist in the [access key configuration](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations).

### Can I use self-hosted models?

Yes.
Create a custom provider for a model running on your machine, private network, or cloud GPU.

See [Use a model you run yourself](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/use-a-model-you-run-yourself).

### What is a custom provider?

A custom provider is an upstream endpoint you define, such as Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio, a private deployment, or another OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic-compatible API.

Custom providers let you call models you run yourself through the same gateway URL as built-in providers.

See [Custom Providers](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/custom-providers).

### Why isn't my custom model working?

Check that:

1. The upstream exposes a supported OpenAI or Anthropic API surface.
2. The custom provider has the correct base URL.
3. The custom provider declares the model ID you're calling.
4. The endpoint is reachable from ngrok.ai.
5. The access key configuration allows the provider and model.
6. Provider credentials are attached if the upstream requires authentication.

See [Use a model you run yourself](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/use-a-model-you-run-yourself).

## Limits

### How big can a request be?

Inference requests, such as chat completions, messages, and embeddings, can be up to 32 MiB on every API format.

File uploads through the [Files API](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/files) can be up to 512 MiB.
Uploads that use ngrok-managed keys also count against your account's file storage limit.

### What happens if my request is too big?

The gateway rejects it with HTTP 413 and [`ERR_NGROK_AI_GATEWAY_REQUEST_BODY_TOO_LONG`](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/error-codes#err_ngrok_ai_gateway_request_body_too_long).
The JSON error body uses the format of the API you called, so your SDK's normal error handling picks it up.
An OpenAI-compatible request gets:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "error": {
    "message": "[ERR_NGROK_AI_GATEWAY_REQUEST_BODY_TOO_LONG] Request body is too long. Max 32 MiB.",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "code": "request_body_too_long"
  }
}
```

To send large documents or images to OpenAI or Anthropic models, upload them once with the [Files API](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/files) and reference them by ID instead of inlining them in every request.

### Can I cap token usage?

Yes.
Set these in [Account Settings](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/account-settings#token-limits):

* `maxInputTokens` rejects a request before it reaches a provider when its estimated input tokens exceed the limit.
* `maxOutputTokens` caps how long a completion can be.

Both are unset by default, which means no cap.
Limits must be greater than zero.

### Does the gateway rate limit my keys or account?

The AI Gateway doesn't set a fixed per-key or per-account limit on request rate or concurrent requests.
Usage is subject to fair use, and ngrok may limit traffic that affects the gateway's availability for other customers.

Providers still enforce their own rate limits.
When a provider returns HTTP 429, the gateway tries another quota pool for the same credential, then an ngrok-managed key if one is available, then the next model.
See [Handle gateway errors](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/error-handling).

### What does a 429 from the gateway mean?

The gateway ran out of candidates to try, and the last provider it tried returned a rate limit.
Retry with exponential backoff.

To make this less likely, [attach more than one provider key](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/key-selection-failover) or [configure fallback models](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/configure-fallback-models).

### Will I see my provider's rate-limit headers?

Yes, when the request uses your own provider key and the provider sends them.
The gateway forwards headers such as OpenAI's `x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens`, so you can throttle on your side.
Requests that use ngrok-managed keys don't include them.

## Failover and timeouts

### How does failover work?

The gateway tries candidates in order.

It can fail over between provider keys for the same provider, then between fallback models listed in the request.
The gateway doesn't retry the same model and provider key combination.
It moves to the next available candidate.

See [Error Handling](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/error-handling).

### How do I configure fallback models?

Use `model` for the primary model and `models` for fallback models.

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "model": "openai:gpt-4o",
  "models": ["anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6"],
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
}
```

The gateway tries the primary model first, then each fallback model in order until one succeeds.

See [Configure fallback models](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/configure-fallback-models).

### Can I set fallbacks on the gateway instead of in each request?

Yes, with a [virtual model](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/virtual-models).
A virtual model is a name you choose, such as `chat-default`, that stands for an ordered list of up to 10 models.
Your apps send the name as `model`, and the gateway tries each model in order until one succeeds.

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "model": "chat-default",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
}
```

To change the models or their order for every client at once, edit the virtual model in app.ngrok.ai or with the [Virtual Models API](/docs/ai-gateway/api-reference/virtual-models/update).
Clients don't change, redeploy, or restart.

On the gateway side, you can also:

* Attach multiple provider keys for the same provider, so the gateway [fails over between keys](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/key-selection-failover) on rate limits, quota limits, or auth errors.
* Use [access key configurations](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations) to control which providers and models each access key can reach.

### Can the gateway fail over to a different provider?

Yes, if the request includes fallback models from different providers, or uses a [virtual model](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/virtual-models) that lists them.

For example, you can try OpenAI first and fall back to Anthropic:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "model": "openai:gpt-4o",
  "models": ["anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6"],
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
}
```

The access key configuration must allow each provider and model.

### How long does the gateway try before giving up?

By default, each upstream attempt can take up to 15 minutes, and the whole request, including every failover attempt, up to 30 minutes.
The gateway makes at most 10 upstream attempts per request.

| Bound | Default | Configurable |
| - | - | - |
| Per-request timeout (one upstream attempt) | 15m | Yes |
| Total timeout (all attempts) | 30m | Yes |
| Stream idle timeout (gap between streamed events) | 30s | No |
| Upstream attempts per request | 10 | No |

Streaming and non-streaming requests use the same defaults.
For a stream, the per-request timeout applies only until the provider sends the first byte.
After that, the stream fails if the provider sends nothing for 30 seconds.
See [Streaming responses](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/account-settings#streaming-responses).

Change the timeouts in [Account Settings](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/account-settings) or with the [gateway configuration API](/docs/ai-gateway/api-reference/gateway-config/update).
You can also set account-wide input and output token limits there.

If the total timeout is reached, the gateway stops trying candidates and returns an error.
See [Handle gateway errors](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/error-handling).

### Can I disable automatic failover?

Not directly.

To narrow failover behavior, use a single provider key per provider, send requests with a single model, avoid fallback models, and set shorter timeouts in [Account Settings](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/account-settings).

### Why am I getting rate limited even with multiple keys?

Check that multiple provider keys are attached to the relevant provider in the access key configuration.

The gateway only fails over between keys that are available to the request.
See [Key selection and failover](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/key-selection-failover).

## Security and privacy

### Does ngrok.ai store request and response bodies?

The gateway processes request and response bodies in memory by default and doesn't store them unless you turn on request capture.

To turn on capture, open **Settings > Data Retention** in app.ngrok.ai and enable **Request Capture**.
Capture stores the request and response headers and bodies for your request and for each attempt the gateway sends to a provider, including streamed responses.
Captures are kept for 30 days and then deleted.
See [Request capture](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/account-settings#request-capture).

The gateway always records request metadata for usage events and debugging, such as token counts, latencies, status codes, providers, and models.

See [Observability](/docs/ai-gateway/observability) for more details.

### How long does ngrok.ai keep my data?

| Data | Retention |
| - | - |
| Captured request and response headers and bodies (only if you turn capture on) | 30 days |
| Usage events (request metadata: tokens, latency, status, provider, model, cost) | 90 days |

### Can I see individual request and response bodies?

Yes, if you've turned on request capture.
Captures are available for 30 days in the [request details panel](/docs/ai-gateway/observability/index#inspect-a-request-in-app-ngrok-ai) on the [Activity](https://app.ngrok.ai/activity) page.

Without capture, usage records include only metadata such as token counts and latency, not full request or response bodies.

See [Observability](/docs/ai-gateway/observability) for what is captured.

### Can I use the gateway for sensitive data?

Yes, but review your own security and compliance requirements.

The AI Gateway doesn't store request and response bodies unless you turn on capture.
If you do, captured bodies are kept for 30 days.
Requests still go to the upstream provider you call, so review the data handling terms for any provider you use.

### How do I redact PII automatically?

Automatic redaction of request and response bodies isn’t available on ngrok.ai just yet.
Captures do redact credential headers, such as `Authorization`, `x-api-key`, and cookies.

Until then, redact any sensitive data in your application before sending it to the gateway.

### How do I secure my gateway when using my own provider keys?

You can store your provider keys safely in app.ngrok.ai, and have your application send only access keys.

You can use access key configurations to control which providers and models each key can call.
If an access key is ever exposed, revoke it and create a new one.

See [Securing Your Gateway](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/securing-endpoints).

## Monitoring and debugging

### How do I view usage and request metrics?

You can check out the **Usage** page in app.ngrok.ai, or query usage events with the AI Gateway API.

Usage events include helpful details like request time, provider, model, token counts, latency, and status.

For more, see [Observability](/docs/ai-gateway/observability).

### How do I debug which provider was used?

Take a look at usage events in [app.ngrok.ai](https://app.ngrok.ai), or query them with the AI Gateway API to see what’s happening behind the scenes.

If you want more predictable routing while debugging, try using `provider:model` in your request, like `openai:gpt-4o`.

### Why are my requests failing silently?

Start with the response status code and error message.

Then check:

1. The access key is valid.
2. The access key configuration allows the requested provider and model.
3. The provider key is present if the provider requires one.
4. The model name is valid.
5. The account has credits.
6. The upstream provider is available.

See [Debugging](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/debugging) and [Error Codes](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/error-codes).

### Does the gateway add latency?

Yes, the gateway can add a small amount of latency for parsing, token counting, routing, and failover decisions.

Provider response time usually dominates total latency.

### How are tokens counted?

The gateway estimates token counts with `tiktoken` and uses provider-reported counts when available.

Token counts appear in [usage events](/docs/ai-gateway/observability#usage-api).

### Can I cache responses to reduce costs?

Not yet.
Response caching isn’t currently available on ngrok.ai, but it’s under consideration for a future release.

## Troubleshooting

### Why am I getting "provider not allowed"?

The requested provider isn’t currently allowed by the access key configuration tied to your access key.

To fix this, you can update the configuration to allow that provider, or send the request using an access key that already has permission to call it.

See [Access Key Configurations](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations) and [Error Codes](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/error-codes).

### Why am I getting "model unknown"?

The gateway couldn't resolve the model for the request.

Common causes include:

* The model isn't in the catalog.
* The model name has a typo.
* The request uses a non-catalog model without a provider prefix.
* The access key configuration doesn't allow the model.

For non-catalog models, use the `provider:model` format:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "model": "openai:gpt-5-preview",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
}
```

### Why is my provider key not working?

Check that:

1. The provider key was added to the correct provider.
2. The key is valid and hasn't expired.
3. The provider account has access to the requested model.
4. The provider account has enough balance or quota.
5. The access key configuration routes requests through that provider key.

If usage isn't appearing in your provider account, the request may be paid with credits instead of using your provider key.

### Why is failover not working?

Start by thinking about the kind of failover you want.

If you're looking for provider key failover, make sure you've attached multiple provider keys for the same provider in your access key configuration.

If you want model or provider failover, include fallback models in your request:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "model": "openai:gpt-4o",
  "models": ["anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6"],
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
}
```

The access key configuration must allow every fallback provider and model.

### Why is the gateway timing out?

The total request time may be hitting the timeout set in [Account Settings](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/account-settings).

Try increasing the total timeout, checking upstream provider latency, or reducing the number of fallback candidates.

A streaming response also fails if the provider sends nothing for 30 seconds.
This limit isn't configurable.

### Why was my request rejected before reaching a provider?

The gateway can reject a request before upstream routing when:

* The access key is missing or invalid.
* The access key configuration doesn't allow the provider or model.
* The model can't be resolved.
* The account has insufficient credits.
* Required provider credentials are missing.

Check the response error code and see [Error Codes](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/error-codes).

## Routing behavior

### Can I route based on request content?

Not at the gateway layer today.

For now, you can use separate access keys and configurations for each client, or handle routing in your application before sending requests to the gateway.

### How do I prioritize certain models or providers?

List fallback models in preference order in the request body.

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "model": "openai:gpt-4o",
  "models": ["anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6"],
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
}
```

To set the order on the gateway instead of in each request, use a [virtual model](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/virtual-models).

For different clients or teams, create separate access keys with different configurations.

### Does the gateway support streaming?

Yes.
Streaming is supported, and the gateway forwards SSE streams transparently.

### What happens if a stream fails partway through?

A stream that fails partway through is billed, because its first bytes were already delivered to your client.
If the provider doesn't report usage for that request, the gateway estimates token counts, and the usage event is marked `usageEstimated: true`.

To see what happened, look up the request by its `Ngrok-AIG-Request-Id` with the [request attempts endpoint](/docs/ai-gateway/api-reference/usage/request-attempts).
See [Handle gateway errors](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/error-handling).

# Set Up an Access Key Configuration
Source: https://ngrok.com/docs/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations

Create an access key configuration that controls which providers and models a key can call and which provider keys it uses.

Every request to `https://gateway.ngrok.ai` must include an [access key](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/access-keys).
Upstream provider credentials are managed in [app.ngrok.ai](https://app.ngrok.ai) and injected server-side based on the access key's **configuration**—see [Access keys vs provider keys](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/access-keys#access-keys-vs-provider-keys).

Access key configurations control:

* **Access scope**: which providers and models the key may call
* **Routing rules**: whether to pay with credits or use your stored [provider keys](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys) for each provider
* **Firewall policy**: which [Firewall](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/firewall) policy checks the key's requests and tool calls

See [Create a configuration](#create-a-configuration) below, or the [Access Key Configurations API](/docs/ai-gateway/api-reference/access-key-configurations/create).

## How it fits together

```mermaid theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
flowchart LR
  App["Your app"] -->|"access key only"| Gateway["gateway.ngrok.ai"]
  Gateway --> Config["Access key configuration"]
  Config --> Ngrok["Pay with credits"]
  Config --> BYOK["Stored provider keys"]
  Ngrok --> OpenAI["OpenAI / Anthropic"]
  BYOK --> Providers["Other built-in or custom providers"]
```

1. Your app sends an **access key** with each request.
2. The gateway loads the configuration linked to that key (or default rules if none is linked).
3. The AI Gateway selects upstream credentials from the configuration's routing rules.

## Default behavior

An access key with **no configuration** (allow-all scope) can reach any provider and model your account supports.
For built-in models you [can pay for with credits](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/model-catalog#billing-and-provider-credentials), an ngrok.ai key is used automatically when you have [credits](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/credits).

To use your own provider accounts, restrict scope, or control failover, create a configuration and assign it to the key.

## Create a configuration

### Via the ngrok dashboard

1. Open [app.ngrok.ai](https://app.ngrok.ai) → **Keys** → **Configurations**.
2. Click **New configuration**.
3. Set a name and optional description.
4. Under **Access**, allow only the providers and models this key should use.
5. Under **Routing**, add a rule per provider:
   * **ngrok**: pay with credits.
     ngrok.ai supplies the credentials ([supported providers](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/model-catalog#billing-and-provider-credentials) only)
   * **Bring your own API key**: attach one or more stored provider keys (tried in order)
6. Save the configuration.
7. On **Keys**, edit an access key and assign the configuration.

### Via the AI Gateway API

Create configurations with the [Access Key Configurations API](/docs/ai-gateway/api-reference/access-key-configurations/create).
Authorize the request with your [AI Gateway API key](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/access-keys#credentials-overview).

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
curl -X POST https://api.ngrok.ai/access-key-configurations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Production OpenAI BYOK",
    "access": {
      "providers": { "allow": ["openai"] },
      "models": { "allow": ["openai/gpt-4o"] }
    },
    "router": {
      "rules": [
        {
          "provider": "openai",
          "steps": [
            {
              "type": "user",
              "keySelectionStrategy": "ordered",
              "keys": [{ "id": "aigpk_xxxxx" }]
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

Link the configuration when creating or updating an access key:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
curl -X PATCH https://api.ngrok.ai/access-keys/aigk_xxxxx \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "accessKeyConfigurationId": "aigac_xxxxx" }'
```

See the [Access Key Configurations API reference](/docs/ai-gateway/api-reference/access-key-configurations/create) and [Access Keys API](/docs/ai-gateway/api-reference/access-keys/update).

## Routing rules

Each routing rule targets exactly one **provider** or one **model** and defines an ordered list of steps.
A model rule uses the provider-qualified form, such as `openai:openai/gpt-5.5`, and takes precedence over a provider rule for the same provider.
A configuration can have at most one rule per provider.

| Step type | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `ngrok` | Pay with credits. ngrok.ai supplies the key ([supported providers](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/model-catalog#billing-and-provider-credentials) only) |
| `user` | Use attached provider keys, tried in list order |

For built-in providers, you can pay with credits, bring your own key, or list your own keys first with an `ngrok` step after them as a fallback.
The gateway uses the first step that has usable credentials.
The `ngrok` fallback only runs when your keys hit auth errors or rate limits.

When a configuration has no rule for a provider, requests to that provider are paid with credits only.
Stored provider keys aren't used without a rule.

Custom providers require a `user` step with at least one provider key when the upstream requires authentication.

## Multi-key failover

Attach multiple provider keys to the same routing rule step.
The gateway tries them in order when a key hits a rate limit or auth error.
Server errors and timeouts move to the next model instead.
See [Multi-key failover](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/key-selection-failover).

## Restrict providers and models

Use the **access** block to limit what an access key can call:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "access": {
    "providers": { "allow": ["openai", "anthropic"] },
    "models": { "allow": ["openai/gpt-4o", "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6"] }
  }
}
```

Omit `access` entirely for allow-all scope.
An empty `allow` array blocks all traffic on that dimension.

# Configure Account Settings
Source: https://ngrok.com/docs/ai-gateway/guides/account-settings

Set default timeouts, token limits, and request capture for every AI Gateway request, from the ngrok.ai dashboard or the API.

Account-wide gateway settings apply to every request through `https://gateway.ngrok.ai`, so you can set defaults like timeouts and token limits once instead of repeating them on every [access key configuration](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations).

## Timeouts

| Setting | Default | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `perRequestTimeout` | `15m` | Max time for a single upstream attempt |
| `totalTimeout` | `30m` | Max time for a request including all failover attempts |

If a single attempt exceeds `perRequestTimeout`, the gateway moves on to the next fallback.
If total time exceeds `totalTimeout`, the gateway returns an error.
`perRequestTimeout` must be less than or equal to `totalTimeout`.

### Streaming responses

Streams use the per-request timeout differently, so a long completion isn't cut off:

* The per-request timeout applies only until the provider sends the first byte.
  After that, the stream fails if the provider sends nothing for 30 seconds.
* The total timeout applies to the whole stream, including the time after the first byte.

> [!WARNING]
>
> A streaming response stops when `totalTimeout` expires.
> If you lower it, make sure it still covers your longest streaming responses.

## Token limits

| Setting | Default | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `maxInputTokens` | none | Reject requests above estimated input tokens |
| `maxOutputTokens` | none | Cap completion length |

Leave token limits unset for no cap.
Set them to block oversized requests before they reach a provider.
Limits must be greater than zero.

`maxOutputTokens` also applies when your request doesn't set an output limit: the gateway adds one.
When your request asks for more, the gateway lowers it to your limit, and to the model's own maximum.

## Request capture

Request capture stores the request and response headers and bodies, including prompts and completions, for your request and each attempt the gateway sends to a provider.
You can inspect them in the [request details panel](/docs/ai-gateway/observability/index#inspect-a-request-in-app-ngrok-ai) on the [Activity](https://app.ngrok.ai/activity) page.
Capture is off by default.

To turn it on:

1. Open [Settings > Data Retention](https://app.ngrok.ai/settings/data-retention) in app.ngrok.ai.
2. Under **Request Capture**, set **Full capture** to **Enabled**.
3. Select **Save**.

![Data Retention settings page in app.ngrok.ai with the Request Capture section, Full capture set to Disabled, and a 30-day retention window](https://mintcdn.com/ngrok/NtlJmMH9rvSW0IRo/ai-gateway/guides/img/data-retention-request-capture.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=NtlJmMH9rvSW0IRo\&q=85\&s=72252f687cbed2705635453e7f599129)

Capture applies to requests from then on. It doesn't fill in requests that were made while it was off.
Set **Full capture** to **Disabled** to stop capturing; only request metadata, such as tokens, latency, and cost, is then recorded.

What capture stores:

* Captures are kept for 30 days and then deleted.
* Each body stores up to 4 MB and each set of headers up to 16 KiB. Anything past the limit isn't stored.
* Headers with these names are redacted, in any letter case: `Authorization`, `Proxy-Authorization`, `Cookie`, `Set-Cookie`, `x-api-key`, `x-goog-api-key`, `api-key`, `api_key`, `apikey`, `access-token`, `access_token`, `accesstoken`, `token`, `bearer`, `secret`, and `password`.
* When the gateway calls a provider with an ngrok-managed key, the provider's response headers are redacted except `Content-Type`.
* Bodies are stored as sent, without redaction. The one exception is embedding vectors in embeddings responses, which are replaced with a placeholder that records the vector's dimensions and a SHA-256 hash.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Redaction matches whole header names only.
> A custom credential header with another name, such as `X-Auth-Token`, is stored as sent, and so is any secret inside a prompt or body.

Request capture is set in app.ngrok.ai only. The `/gateway-config` API doesn't read or change it.

## Via dashboard

1. Open [Settings](https://app.ngrok.ai/settings) in app.ngrok.ai
2. On **General**, edit **Total timeout**, **Per-request timeout**, and optional token limits
3. Save

**General** also shows the gateway URL (`https://gateway.ngrok.ai`).
The other Settings pages are **Data Retention** for [request capture](#request-capture), **Admin API Keys** for [AI Gateway API keys](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/access-keys#credentials-overview), and **Account**, which links to [dashboard.ngrok.com](https://dashboard.ngrok.com) for your account details and team members.

## Via the AI Gateway API

Get current settings:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
curl https://api.ngrok.ai/gateway-config \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY"
```

Update settings (omitted fields keep their current values):

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
curl -X PATCH https://api.ngrok.ai/gateway-config \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "perRequestTimeout": "60s",
    "maxInputTokens": 128000,
    "maxOutputTokens": 8192
  }'
```

Clear a token limit by sending `null`:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
curl -X PATCH https://api.ngrok.ai/gateway-config \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "maxInputTokens": null }'
```

Duration fields use Go duration strings (for example, `30s`, `2m`).

See the [Gateway configuration API reference](/docs/ai-gateway/api-reference/gateway-config/get).

# Bring Your Own Provider Key
Source: https://ngrok.com/docs/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys

Add your own provider API key to ngrok.ai, use an access key configuration to choose which access keys can use it, and rotate it safely.

Use provider keys to let ngrok.ai call an upstream provider with your own credentials.

Provider keys are the API keys you already use with OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, and others. You can add them to ngrok.ai once, and it uses them to call those providers on your behalf, keeping keys out of your app.

> [!NOTE]
>
> For [certain providers](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/model-catalog#billing-and-provider-credentials), like OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and DeepSeek, you can skip provider keys and [pay with credits](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/pay-with-credits) instead.

## Add a provider key

### Via the ngrok dashboard

**1. Open Providers**

Head over to the [Providers](https://app.ngrok.ai/providers) page and choose the provider you want from either the **Built-in** or **Custom** tab.

**2. Add a key**

Once you're on the provider's page, scroll down to **API keys** and add your key there.

### Via the AI Gateway API

You can add your own API Keys for providers via the [Provider Keys API](/docs/ai-gateway/api-reference/provider-keys/create):

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
curl -X POST https://api.ngrok.ai/provider-keys \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "providerId": "openai",
    "name": "My OpenAI Key",
    "value": "sk-proj-..."
  }'
```

After you add a key, the dashboard only shows a redacted version (`first10***last4`). Make sure you keep a copy of the full key from your provider, since you won’t be able to see it again here. Provider keys are shared across your account, so you can use the same key with multiple access keys.

> [!NOTE]
>
> When a key does not have an access configuration attached, the gateway begins using this provider key immediately.
> To select specific keys, define failover order, or restrict providers and models, use an access key configuration.

## Control access with a configuration

An access key without a configuration uses any provider keys you've added, so it works out of the box.

If you need more control, you can attach an [access key configuration](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations). This lets you choose which key to use, set a fallback order, or limit which providers and models are available.

### 1. Add the provider key

First, make sure you've already [added a key](#add-a-provider-key) for the provider.

### 2. Attach the key in an access key configuration

Next, go to your [access key configuration](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations#create-a-configuration). Then add a routing rule for the provider, choose **Bring your own API key**, and pick the key you added in the previous step.

You can add more than one key for the same provider—if one fails or hits a limit, the gateway will automatically try the next one in your list. For more details, see [key selection and failover](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/key-selection-failover).

When using the ngrok.ai API, reference the key's ID in the configuration's router rules:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "router": {
    "rules": [
      {
        "provider": "openai",
        "steps": [
          {
            "type": "user",
            "keySelectionStrategy": "ordered",
            "keys": [{ "id": "aigpk_xxxxx" }]
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### 3. Assign the configuration to an access key

Navigate to the [Access Keys](https://app.ngrok.ai/keys) page, and assign the configuration to the [access key](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/access-keys) your app uses.

### 4. Send a request

Your app only needs to send the access key. The gateway uses it to find the right configuration, chooses the provider key, and makes the request for you:

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1",
    api_key="ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx"  # Access key, not the provider key
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-4o",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]
)
```

## Rotating provider keys

[Rotating provider keys](/docs/ai-gateway/api-reference/provider-keys/rotate) lets you update its value without changing its ID, so anything already using it keeps working. This means you can keep your existing configurations as they are.

### 1. Rotate the key

Update the key by sending its new value to the [Provider Keys API](/docs/ai-gateway/api-reference/provider-keys/rotate), using your [ngrok.ai API key](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/access-keys#credentials-overview):

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
curl -X POST https://api.ngrok.ai/provider-keys/aigpk_xxxxx/rotate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "My OpenAI Key",
    "value": "sk-proj-..."
  }'
```

### 2. Verify traffic

Send a test request with your access key. The key ID is unchanged, so there's nothing else to update.

## Common issues

| Problem | What to check |
| - | - |
| Request is rejected before routing | The access key configuration may not allow the provider or model |
| Provider returns an auth error | The provider key may be missing, invalid, expired, or unable to call the requested model |
| Usage is not appearing in provider billing | The request may be paid with credits instead of using your provider key |

# Automatic Model Selection
Source: https://ngrok.com/docs/ai-gateway/guides/automatic-model-selection

Use ngrok/auto to let ngrok.ai pick the cheapest model that can handle each prompt, and see which model answered.

Set the model to `ngrok/auto` when you want ngrok.ai to choose the model for each request.
ngrok.ai reads the prompt, estimates how capable a model it needs, and tries the models your access key can reach in that order, starting with the cheapest model that fits.

Use it when your traffic mixes simple and hard prompts and you'd rather not pay top-model prices for "hello" or a unit conversion.

## Send a request

Set `model` to `ngrok/auto`:

```python Python highlight={9} theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1",
    api_key="ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx",  # Your access key
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="ngrok/auto",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Explain the difference between TCP and UDP."}],
)

print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
curl https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "ngrok/auto",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Explain the difference between TCP and UDP."}]
  }'
```

On Chat Completions (`/v1/chat/completions`), Responses (`/v1/responses`), and Messages (`/v1/messages`), leaving out `model` entirely has the same effect.
Most SDKs require a model, so `ngrok/auto` is the clearer choice.

`ngrok/auto` also works on these endpoints:

| Endpoint | How to ask for `ngrok/auto` |
| - | - |
| Gemini `generateContent` | Put it in the path: `/v1beta/models/ngrok/auto:generateContent` |
| Gemini Interactions (`/v1beta/interactions`) | `"model": "ngrok/auto"` in the body |
| OpenAI Decisions (`/v1/decisions`) | `"model": "ngrok/auto"`. Only `gpt-6-luna` serves Decisions, so this always picks it. See [Typed-question APIs](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/decisions-and-system-one) |

## How ngrok.ai picks the model

ngrok.ai sorts models into three price bands by what they charge per million input tokens:

| Band | Input price |
| - | - |
| Low | Under \$1 per million tokens |
| Medium | \$1 to under \$5 per million tokens |
| High | \$5 or more per million tokens |

On Chat Completions and Messages, ngrok.ai first asks a small classifier model how much capability the prompt needs:

* **Simple prompts**, like greetings, common facts, short rewrites, or a regex, go to the low band.
* **Ordinary professional work**, like writing or fixing a small program, a SQL query, or summarizing a document, goes to the medium band. If that work needs little step-by-step reasoning, it goes to the high band instead, because the answer depends more on writing quality.
* **Hard prompts**, like multi-step reasoning, competition-style math, rigorous proofs, or expert analysis, go to the high band.

If the classifier can't answer quickly, the request starts at the low band instead of failing.

On the other endpoints, ngrok.ai doesn't classify the prompt, so every request starts at the low band.

### The order models are tried in

Once ngrok.ai has a band, it orders every model your access key can use:

1. Models from [custom providers](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/custom-providers) you've added a provider key for.
2. The models that do best on that kind of prompt.
3. The rest of the band, cheapest first.
4. The bands above, cheapest first.
5. The bands below, cheapest first.
6. Models with no published price.

The band sets where the list starts, not which models are allowed. If the first model fails, the gateway [fails over](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/error-handling) down the list the same way it does for any other request.

### Reasoning effort

On Chat Completions and Messages, the classifier also picks a reasoning effort: low, medium, or high.
For each model that has a reasoning setting the gateway can set, such as `reasoning_effort` or Anthropic's adaptive thinking effort, that level replaces any reasoning setting you sent.
Models without one get your request unchanged.

If the classifier can't decide, your own reasoning settings apply.

## See which model answered

Read the `Ngrok-AIG-Model` [response header](/docs/ai-gateway/how-it-works#response-headers).
It names the model that produced the response.
The `model` field in the response body comes from the provider, so use the header when you need to know what answered.

The models ngrok.ai prefers can change as new models launch and prices move, so don't depend on a particular model being picked.

## Access key configurations still apply

`ngrok/auto` only picks from models the access key can already reach:

* The [access key configuration](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations) must allow the provider and model.
* The model needs usable credentials: you [pay with credits](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/pay-with-credits) or have [your own provider key](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys) routed to it.
* The model must support the endpoint you called.
* The model catalog must mark the model as available to `ngrok/auto`. Narrow-purpose models, such as translation or classifier models, and models past their deprecation date are left out.

To keep `ngrok/auto` inside a set of providers or models, [restrict the access key](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/restrict-providers-and-models).

If none of the models the key can reach qualify, the request fails with [`ERR_NGROK_27227`](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/error-codes#err_ngrok_27227). Name a model in the request instead.

## Combining with fallback models

`ngrok/auto` and a [`models` fallback list](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/configure-fallback-models) are two different ways to pick models, so don't use them together:

* On Chat Completions and Messages, if you list real models alongside `ngrok/auto`, the gateway ignores `ngrok/auto` and uses your list as an ordinary fallback list.
* On the Gemini endpoints, combining them returns `ERR_NGROK_27228` with the message `Invalid request: models cannot be combined with ngrok/auto`.

## Billing

You pay for the model that served the response, the same as if you'd named it.

The classifier isn't billed as model usage. Its input tokens count toward the [processing fee](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/credits#processing-fee) on that request, whether you pay with credits or use your own provider keys.
Requests on endpoints that skip the classifier add nothing extra.

# Configure Fallback Models
Source: https://ngrok.com/docs/ai-gateway/guides/configure-fallback-models

List fallback models in a request so the AI Gateway can retry on another model or provider, such as a hosted backup for a private model.

Use fallback models when you want the AI Gateway to try another model if the primary request fails.

Fallback is useful when you want better availability across providers, or when you want to try a private model first and use a hosted model as a backup.

## Add fallback models

Set the primary model with `model`.
Set fallback models with `models`.

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "model": "gpt-4o",
  "models": ["gpt-4o-mini", "anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6"],
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
}
```

The gateway tries `gpt-4o` first.
If that request fails with a rate limit, an auth error, a server error, or a timeout, it tries each entry in `models` in order until one succeeds.
Other 4xx errors, such as an invalid request, return right away.
See [what triggers failover](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/error-handling).

## Choose the provider for each fallback

Fallback models can use model IDs or `provider:model`.

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "model": "openai:gpt-4o",
  "models": [
    "openai:gpt-4o-mini",
    "anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6"
  ],
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
}
```

Use provider-qualified model names when you want to control exactly which provider each fallback uses.

## Fall back from a private model to a hosted model

Fallback works with [custom providers](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/custom-providers), too.

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "model": "my-ollama:llama3.2",
  "models": ["openai:gpt-4o-mini"],
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
}
```

In this example, the gateway tries your `my-ollama` provider first.
If that request fails, it falls back to OpenAI.

## Choose fallback models carefully

Pick fallback models that can handle the same kind of request as the primary model.
Check each model for:

* Input modality.
* Tool calling support.
* Output size.
* Context window.
* Latency expectations.
* Provider credentials.

Use the [model catalog](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/model-catalog) to compare built-in model capabilities.

## Access restrictions still apply

The [access key configuration](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations) assigned to the access key must allow your fallback models.

If a fallback model isn't allowed, the gateway skips it and names it in the `Ngrok-AIG-Rejected-Models` response header.
The request still runs with the models that are allowed.
It fails only when none of the models you listed are allowed.

## Save a fallback list as a virtual model

To keep the list out of your code, save it as a [virtual model](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/virtual-models) and send its name as `model`.
You can then change the models and their order from the gateway, without changing your requests.
This also works for a client that can't send a `models` array.
A virtual model follows the same failover rules as a `models` list.

# Choose How to Reach Providers
Source: https://ngrok.com/docs/ai-gateway/guides/configuring-providers

Compare paying with credits, bringing your own provider key, and connecting a model you run yourself, then follow the guide for your choice.

The AI Gateway can reach providers in three ways. Pick the path that matches what you're trying to do.

## Use a provider without a provider account

Use [credits](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/credits) when you want the fastest path to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, or another [provider you can pay for with credits](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/model-catalog#billing-and-provider-credentials). The gateway supplies upstream credentials and bills model usage through your credit balance.

Start here: [Pay with credits](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/pay-with-credits).

## Bring your own provider key

Bring your own key when you want model usage billed to your provider account, need a provider that requires your own credentials, or want to use your own provider account.

Start here: [Bring your own provider key](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys).

## Use a model you run yourself

Use a custom provider when your model runs on your machine, private network, cloud GPU, or another OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible endpoint outside the built-in catalog.

Start here: [Use a model you run yourself](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/use-a-model-you-run-yourself).

## Make the provider usable from a request

Adding a provider or provider key doesn't route traffic by itself. A working request needs:

1. A provider: built-in or custom.
2. A credential source: credits or a provider key, when required.
3. An [access key configuration](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations) that allows the provider and model.
4. An [access key](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/access-keys) assigned to that configuration.
5. A request with a matching `model` or `provider:model`.

If requests are rejected before they reach the provider, check [Restrict providers and models](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/restrict-providers-and-models).

# Debug Failed Requests
Source: https://ngrok.com/docs/ai-gateway/guides/debugging

Find out why an AI Gateway request failed from its request ID, error code, and response headers, and fix the most common errors.

When troubleshooting a request to `https://gateway.ngrok.ai`:

1. Record the `Ngrok-AIG-Request-Id` [response header](/docs/ai-gateway/how-it-works#response-headers). Every response carries it, errors included, and it identifies the request in usage data.
2. Check the error code and message in the response body. See [Error Codes](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/error-codes).
3. Read `Ngrok-AIG-Attempts` to see whether failover ran. A count above 1 means the gateway tried more than one upstream candidate before it gave up, so the cause is upstream rather than in your request. An absent header means the request failed before any attempt, which points at the request body or the access key configuration.
4. Verify your app sends an [access key](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/access-keys)—not an upstream provider key.
5. Confirm the access key's [configuration](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations) allows the provider and model you requested, with routing credentials attached.
6. Look the request up in the dashboard at [app.ngrok.ai](https://app.ngrok.ai), or query it with the [Usage API](/docs/ai-gateway/observability#usage-api).

Common fixes:

| Symptom | Check |
| - | - |
| 401 Unauthorized | Access key missing, malformed, or deleted |
| 402 Payment Required (27206) | Out of credits: [purchase credits](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/credits). This happens even if you use your own provider keys |
| No keys available for provider (27202) | Configuration missing a routing rule or provider keys for the requested provider |
| Provider or model not allowed by the access policy (27231, 27232) | Model or provider blocked by the configuration's access scope |
| Every model failed | The response carries the last model's error. Read `Ngrok-AIG-Attempts` and the attempt chain. See [Handle gateway errors](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/error-handling) |
| Response names a model you did not expect | Read `Ngrok-AIG-Model`, not the `model` field in the body. The body is passed through byte-for-byte and keeps the provider's own wording |

See [Handle gateway errors](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/error-handling) for retry and failover behavior.


# Typed-Question APIs
Source: https://ngrok.com/docs/ai-gateway/guides/decisions-and-system-one

Send typed questions to OpenAI Decisions and Typesafe AI System One through ngrok.ai and get back typed answers instead of chat replies.

Some models don't chat.
You send them some input and a list of typed questions, and they send back a typed answer to each one, such as true or false, one choice from a list, or a score.
That's useful for routing support tickets, flagging content, or scoring urgency without parsing free-form text.

ngrok.ai serves two of these APIs:

| API | Endpoint | Provider | Models |
| - | - | - | - |
| [OpenAI Decisions](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/decisions) | `POST /v1/decisions` | OpenAI | `gpt-6-luna` |
| [Typesafe AI System One](https://docs.typesafe.ai) | `POST /v1/systemone` | [Typesafe AI](/docs/ai-gateway/providers/typesafeai) | `jev-latest`, `jev-preview`, `jev-1.13.0` |
| System One | `POST /v1/systemone` | [Liquid AI](/docs/ai-gateway/providers/liquid) | `d1`, `d1.1`, `d1-ultra` |

You can [pay with credits](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/pay-with-credits) for all of them, or [bring your own provider key](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys) for OpenAI, Typesafe AI, or Liquid AI.

## Decisions requests

A Decisions request has an `input`, in the same message format as the Responses API, and an array of `questions`.
Each question has a `type` (`predicate`, `choice`, or `score`), a `name`, and `instructions`.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
curl https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1/decisions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-6-luna",
    "input": [
      {
        "role": "user",
        "content": [
          {"type": "input_text", "text": "I was charged twice for my March invoice and need one charge refunded today."}
        ]
      }
    ],
    "questions": [
      {"type": "predicate", "name": "is_refund_request", "instructions": "Does the customer ask for a refund?"},
      {
        "type": "choice",
        "name": "team",
        "instructions": "Which team owns this ticket?",
        "choices": [
          {"value": "billing", "description": "Charges, invoices, and refunds."},
          {"value": "technical", "description": "Product defects and outages."}
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

The response has an `answers` array with one entry per question.
A `predicate` answer has the `probability` that it's true.
A `choice` answer names the `choice` it picked, with a probability for each option:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "model": "gpt-6-luna",
  "answers": [
    {"type": "predicate", "name": "is_refund_request", "probability": 1.0},
    {
      "type": "choice",
      "name": "team",
      "choice": "billing",
      "probabilities": [
        {"value": "billing", "probability": 1.0},
        {"value": "technical", "probability": 0.0}
      ],
      "confidence": 1.0
    }
  ],
  "usage": {"input_tokens": 286, "output_tokens": 0, "total_tokens": 286}
}
```

The gateway forwards `model`, `input`, `questions`, and `safety_identifier`.
It removes any other top-level field and names it in the `Ngrok-AIG-Removed-Params` [response header](/docs/ai-gateway/how-it-works#response-headers).
See [OpenAI's Decisions guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/decisions) for every question type and option.

`"model": "ngrok/auto"` also works and always picks `gpt-6-luna`.
Any other model returns [`ERR_NGROK_27226`](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/error-codes#err_ngrok_27226), because no other model serves Decisions.

When you pay with credits, OpenAI bills a decision on input tokens only, at `gpt-6-luna`'s input rate.

## Typesafe AI requests

A System One request has a `state`, the text to evaluate, and a `questions` object that maps each question ID to a typed question.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
curl https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1/systemone \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "jev-latest",
    "state": "The server returned 500 for every request for ten minutes.",
    "questions": {
      "is_urgent": {
        "type": "noul",
        "instructions": "Is this an urgent production incident?"
      }
    }
  }'
```

The response maps each question ID to its answer, with a calibrated probability:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "model": "jev-1.13.0",
  "answers": {"is_urgent": {"type": "noul", "noul": 0.91}},
  "usage": {"input_tokens": 287, "output_tokens": 23}
}
```

The gateway forwards `model`, `state`, and `questions`, and removes any other top-level field.
See the [Typesafe AI API reference](https://docs.typesafe.ai) for question types such as `choice` and `score`, and the [Typesafe AI provider page](/docs/ai-gateway/providers/typesafeai) for setup.

Name a Jev model in the request.
`ngrok/auto` doesn't pick Jev models, so it returns [`ERR_NGROK_27227`](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/error-codes#err_ngrok_27227) on this endpoint.

## What's different from chat requests

Both APIs differ from Chat Completions and Messages in a few ways:

* **No streaming**: A request with `"stream": true` returns `ERR_NGROK_27228` before reaching the provider.
* **No fallback list**: The gateway reads only `model`, so a `models` list is removed rather than used.
* **POST only**: Each API has a single create endpoint.
  Other methods and paths below it return an error.
* **Same billing model**: Every request pays the [processing fee](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/credits#processing-fee).
  When you pay with credits, credits also cover the model cost.

# Handle Gateway Errors
Source: https://ngrok.com/docs/ai-gateway/guides/error-handling

Understand which failures the AI Gateway retries, the order it tries candidates in, and how timeouts bound the whole request.

When an upstream attempt fails, the AI Gateway either moves to another candidate or stops and returns the error.
This page explains which failures it retries, in what order, and what bounds the retrying.

## What triggers failover

The gateway moves to another candidate on these failures:

* Authentication failures: HTTP 401 or 403 because the provider rejected the key.
  A 401 or 403 for any other reason stops the request.
* Rate limits: HTTP 429.
* Server errors: HTTP 500 and above.
* Request timeouts: HTTP 408, or the attempt exceeding your per-request timeout.
* Network failures: connection errors, DNS failures, and TLS errors.

Any other 4xx response stops the request immediately.
A malformed request or an unsupported parameter isn't going to succeed on a different provider, so the gateway returns the error rather than spending your quota on it.

## Failover order

Where the gateway goes next depends on how the attempt failed.

| Failure | Order the gateway tries |
| - | - |
| 401 or 403 | Next provider key for the same provider, then an ngrok-managed key if one is available, then the next model |
| 429 | A different quota pool for the credential, then an ngrok-managed key if one is available, then the next model |
| 500 and above, 408, or a network failure | The next model |

Model candidates come from the `model` field first, then the `models` array in order:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "model": "gpt-4o",
  "models": ["anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-5", "google:gemini-3.6-flash"],
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
}
```

If `model` or an entry in `models` is a [virtual model](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/virtual-models), the gateway replaces it with the models it stands for, in order.
Those models follow the same failover rules as any other candidate.

The gateway never retries the same model and key combination, except in the one case below.

A bare model ID, such as `gpt-4o`, also expands to every provider that serves that model.
The model author's own provider goes first, then resellers such as OpenRouter.
A `provider:model` ID, such as `openai:gpt-4o`, reaches only that provider.

> [!NOTE]
>
> To fail over to a different model, list it in the `models` array, or set it up as a [fallback model](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/configure-fallback-models).

### Retrying the same provider

When a provider answers 429 or 503 with a `Retry-After` header, the gateway waits and retries the same backend instead of moving on.
It does that only when the wait is 5 seconds or less, only when the wait still fits inside your total timeout, and at most twice per request.
Otherwise it treats the response as a rate limit or a server error and moves to the next candidate.

## What bounds the retrying

Two timeouts and an attempt cap bound every request:

| Bound | Default | What it limits |
| - | - | - |
| Per-request timeout | 15m | A single upstream attempt |
| Total timeout | 30m | The whole request, including every attempt and any `Retry-After` wait |
| Attempt cap | 10 | Upstream attempts per client request. Not configurable. |

Streams work differently after the first byte.
See [Streaming responses](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/account-settings#streaming-responses).

Set the timeouts for your account in [Account Settings](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/account-settings), or through the [Configuration API](/docs/ai-gateway/api-reference/gateway-config/get).
When the total timeout is reached, failover stops even if candidates remain, and the gateway returns `ERR_NGROK_3810`.

## Failures that never reach failover

Some requests fail before the gateway makes any upstream attempt.
These return immediately, and the response carries no `Ngrok-AIG-Attempts` header:

* The request body couldn't be parsed.
* The model is unknown, or the model address is malformed.
* The requested provider or model is blocked by the access key configuration's access scope.
* No provider key is available for the requested provider.
* The account has no credits.
  This happens even if you use your own provider keys.

None of these are billed.
The gateway bills an attempt only once its response reaches your client, so a request that never reached a provider costs nothing.
A stream that fails partway through is billed, because its first bytes were already delivered.

See [Error Codes](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/error-codes) for the code each of these returns.

## Best practices

1. **Attach several provider keys** per provider so an exhausted credential fails over instead of failing the request.
   See [Multi-key failover](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/key-selection-failover).
2. **List candidates from more than one provider** so a provider-wide outage has somewhere to go.
3. **Set timeouts to match your latency budget.**
   A total timeout that is too tight cuts failover short; one that is too loose makes a slow failure look like a hang.
4. **Record `Ngrok-AIG-Request-Id` from every response** so you can look a failure up afterwards.
   See [Debug failed requests](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/debugging).
