# Find Out Why a Request Failed Over
Source: https://ngrok.com/docs/ai-gateway/guides/why-a-request-failed-over

Trace one AI Gateway request through every upstream attempt to see which providers it tried, in what order, and which one served it.

The AI Gateway may make several attempts before returning a response. The response alone doesn’t show how many attempts were made. This guide shows you how to use a response header to find each attempt and see what happened.

## 1. Read the attempt count off the response

Every response where the gateway tried at least one provider includes the `Ngrok-AIG-Attempts` header, which shows how many attempts were made. A value greater than `1` means the first attempt failed and the gateway tried again.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
curl -i https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $NGROK_AI_ACCESS_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-4o",
    "models": ["anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-5", "google:gemini-3.6-flash"],
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
  }'
```

```http theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
HTTP/2 200
ngrok-aig-request-id: rq_2abcDEF456
ngrok-aig-attempts: 3
ngrok-aig-model: gemini-3.6-flash
```

The AI Gateway made three attempts. The third candidate in the list handled the request after the first two candidates failed.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Use the `Ngrok-AIG-Model` response header to identify the model that handled your request.
> The AI Gateway passes the provider’s response body through unchanged, including its `model` field.
> If the gateway switches models after a failed attempt, these values may differ.
> Use the header as the source of truth.

## 2. Look the request up by ID

Pass the `Ngrok-AIG-Request-Id` value to the attempts endpoint:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
curl https://api.ngrok.ai/usage/requests/rq_2abcDEF456 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY"
```

You get every upstream attempt for that request, ordered by attempt number:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "uri": "https://api.ngrok.ai/usage/requests/rq_2abcDEF456",
  "requestId": "rq_2abcDEF456",
  "attempts": [
    {
      "event": {
        "attemptNumber": 1,
        "provider": "openai",
        "model": "gpt-4o",
        "statusCode": 401,
        "isError": true,
        "keySource": "user"
      },
      "served": false,
      "retryAction": "next_key",
      "completion": "failed",
      "upstreamDurationMs": 88
    },
    {
      "event": {
        "attemptNumber": 2,
        "provider": "openai",
        "model": "gpt-4o",
        "statusCode": 429,
        "isError": true,
        "keySource": "user"
      },
      "served": false,
      "retryAction": "next_backend",
      "completion": "failed",
      "upstreamDurationMs": 214
    },
    {
      "event": {
        "attemptNumber": 3,
        "provider": "anthropic",
        "model": "claude-sonnet-4-6",
        "statusCode": 200,
        "isError": false,
        "keySource": "ngrok"
      },
      "served": true,
      "retryAction": "succeeded",
      "completion": "succeeded",
      "upstreamDurationMs": 1902
    }
  ]
}
```

This endpoint lets you only view requests from your account. It cannot modify them. If a request belongs to another account, the endpoint returns “not found” instead of “forbidden.”

## 3. Check why the AI Gateway retried or stopped

For each attempt, check `completion` to see how it ended and `retryAction` to see what the AI Gateway decided to do next. Use `served` to identify the attempt that returned the response to your client.

### Identify the attempt that returned the response

Look for `served: true`. At most one attempt per request has this value.

Do not assume the last attempt returned a response. A request can end with a failed attempt that did not produce a response for your client.

### Check how each attempt ended

The `completion` field has one of these values:

* `succeeded`
* `failed`
* `timed_out`
* `stream_failed`
* `unknown`

For failed attempts, read the error details to find the cause, then check `retryAction` to understand why the gateway retried or stopped.

### Follow the retry decisions

| `retryAction` | What happened |
| - | - |
| `succeeded` | The attempt produced the response your client received. |
| `next_key` | The credential failed authentication, so the gateway tried the next key for the same provider. |
| `next_quota_pool` | The credential’s quota pool was exhausted, so the gateway moved to another pool. |
| `next_backend` | The provider or model failed, so the gateway tried the next model in the failover list. |
| `managed_fallback` | A customer-owned key failed, so the gateway switched to an ngrok-managed key. |
| `retry_same_backend` | The provider requested a retry using `Retry-After`, so the gateway waited and retried the same backend. |
| `fail_fast` | The failure could not be retried, so the gateway stopped. |
| `exhausted` | No candidates remained to try. |

`retryAction` is optional. It is absent from attempts recorded before the gateway began storing retry decisions.

In the example above, `next_key` on attempt 1 means the first OpenAI key failed authentication, so the gateway tried the second OpenAI key. That key hit a rate limit and no keys were left, so `next_backend` on attempt 2 means the gateway moved to the next model in the failover list. Check each attempt’s error details to see why it failed.

## What this tells you to change

| Pattern down the chain | What to do |
| - | - |
| `next_key` on every OpenAI attempt | Add more [provider keys](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys) for that provider, or raise your quota with them |
| `next_backend` on the first candidate every time | Your primary model is the wrong default. Reorder the [fallback list](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/configure-fallback-models) |
| A single `fail_fast` attempt | The request itself was rejected. Check the status code and the [error code](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/error-codes); failover would not have helped |
| `exhausted` at the end | Every candidate failed. Widen the candidate list or attach credentials for more providers |
| `managed_fallback` you did not expect | Your own key is failing and ngrok.ai credits are absorbing the traffic. Check the key |

## What this endpoint does not include

This endpoint does not include captured request and response bodies, which could contain sensitive information.

# How It Works
Source: https://ngrok.com/docs/ai-gateway/how-it-works

Follow a request from your app through the ngrok AI Gateway to see how it's authenticated, routed to a model, and retried when a provider fails.

## Request flow

When you send a request to `https://gateway.ngrok.ai`:

```mermaid theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant Gateway as gateway.ngrok.ai
    participant Provider as AI Provider

    Client->>Gateway: POST /v1/chat/completions (access key)
    Gateway->>Gateway: Validate access key
    Gateway->>Gateway: Apply configuration and select model
    Gateway->>Provider: Forward request (injected credentials)
    Provider-->>Gateway: Response (or error)
    Gateway-->>Client: Return response
```

1. **Your app sends a request** with your [access key](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/access-keys) to `https://gateway.ngrok.ai`
2. **The gateway validates the key** and loads its [access key configuration](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations)
3. **The gateway resolves the model** from your request body
4. **Provider credentials are selected** from the configuration's routing rules: a key ngrok.ai supplies when you pay with credits, or your stored [provider keys](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys)
5. **The request is translated** when the chosen model doesn't serve your SDK's API format.
   See [Use any model with any SDK](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/use-any-model-with-any-sdk)
6. **Unsupported parameters are stripped** for the chosen model before forwarding, and listed in the `Ngrok-AIG-Removed-Params` [response header](#response-headers) and in [Request details](/docs/ai-gateway/observability/index#inspect-a-request-in-app-ngrok-ai) in app.ngrok.ai
7. **The request is forwarded** to the upstream provider
8. **On failure, the gateway retries** with the next provider key or model candidate
9. **The response is returned** to your app, in your SDK's API format, and usage is recorded

Manage keys, configurations, providers, and credits at [app.ngrok.ai](https://app.ngrok.ai).
Your apps send traffic to `gateway.ngrok.ai`.

## Authentication

Every request must include a valid **access key**.
Send it as `Authorization: Bearer ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx` (OpenAI-compatible APIs) or `x-api-key` (Anthropic native API).

Provider keys stay in [app.ngrok.ai](https://app.ngrok.ai).
The AI Gateway injects those from your configuration after validating the access key.

## Response headers

Every response from `gateway.ngrok.ai` carries ngrok's own headers describing how the gateway handled the request.

| Header | Value | When present |
| - | - | - |
| `Ngrok-AIG-Request-Id` | The request's ID. Use it to look the request up afterwards. | Every response, including rejections and errors. |
| `Ngrok-AIG-Attempts` | How many upstream attempts the gateway made. | Once the gateway tries a provider, on both success and failure. Absent when the request failed before any attempt, such as a malformed body or an unknown model. |
| `Ngrok-AIG-Model` | The upstream model that produced the response. | Success only. |
| `Ngrok-AIG-Rejected-Models` | Comma-separated models from your request that never ran, for example because the access scope blocks them or no credentials are available. Lists at most 4 models. | Once the gateway tries a provider, when at least one requested model was dropped. |
| `Ngrok-AIG-Removed-Params` | Comma-separated request fields the gateway didn't send to the provider that served the response, because that provider or model doesn't support them. | Success only, when the gateway removed at least one field. |
| `Ngrok-AIG-Firewall-Request` | The result of [Firewall](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/firewall) request rules, such as `flagged; rules=force-push`. | When a Firewall policy with request rules checks the request. |
| `Ngrok-AIG-Firewall` | `unscreened` and a reason, when Firewall let traffic through without checking it. | When a Firewall policy applies but couldn't check the request or response. |

All of these are exposed through CORS, so browser clients can read them.
See the [Firewall reference](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/firewall#response-headers) for every Firewall header value.

These are ngrok's headers rather than the provider's, so a managed-key caller and a [Bring Your Own Keys](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/bring-your-own-keys) caller see the same values.
Provider rate-limit headers behave differently: the gateway forwards those only when the attempt used your own provider key.

### The model header is authoritative

The gateway passes the response body through byte-for-byte, unless a [Firewall](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/firewall) policy blocks a tool call or adds `safeguard_results`, or the gateway [translated the request](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/use-any-model-with-any-sdk) into another API format.
The `model` or `modelVersion` field inside the body is the provider's own word, and the gateway doesn't change it to name the model that served the response.
On a multi-model failover the body can therefore name a different model than the header.
Read `Ngrok-AIG-Model` when you need to know what answered.

### Streamed responses

On a streamed response the headers commit with the first flushed byte.
The attempt count is final at that point, because the gateway can't retry once bytes have reached your client.

### Trace IDs aren't a substitute

`Ngrok-Trace-Id` is emitted only when the trace is sampled, it isn't exposed through CORS, and it identifies the whole client request rather than a single attempt.
Use `Ngrok-AIG-Request-Id` to identify a request.

## Model selection

The gateway determines which model and provider to use from your request.

| Model in request | What happens |
| - | - |
| `gpt-4o` | Catalog lookup → OpenAI first, then other providers that serve the same model |
| `openai:gpt-4o` | Explicit OpenAI routing |
| `your-provider:your-model` | A [model you run yourself](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/use-a-model-you-run-yourself) |
| `models` array | Fail over through listed models in order |
| `chat-default` | A [virtual model](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/virtual-models) you saved → fail over through its models in order |
| `ngrok/auto` | ngrok.ai picks a model for each request. See [Automatic model selection](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/automatic-model-selection) |

To choose model IDs and provider-qualified model names, see [Choose a model](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/model-selection-strategies).

## Access key configurations

Configurations define:

* **Access scope**: allowed providers and models
* **Routing rules**: pay with credits or use your own provider keys, per provider

When a configuration has no routing rule for a provider, requests to that provider are paid with credits only.
Stored provider keys aren't used without a rule.

An access key without a configuration uses allow-all scope.
Built-in models you can [pay for with credits](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/model-catalog#billing-and-provider-credentials) use an ngrok.ai key by default when you have [credits](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/credits).

## Failover

The gateway retries automatically when upstream requests fail.

### What triggers failover?

* Rate limits (HTTP 429)
* Auth errors (HTTP 401 or 403) because the provider rejected the key
* Timeouts, server errors (HTTP 5xx), and connection failures

Other 4xx errors return to your client right away, because another model would fail the same way.

### Failover order

What the gateway tries next depends on the error:

* **Auth error or rate limit**: the next provider key in the routing rule step.
  When no keys are left and the rule has an `ngrok` step after the **Bring your own API key** step, the gateway falls back to paying with credits.
* **Timeout, server error, or connection failure**: the gateway skips the remaining keys for that provider and moves to the next model.

The next model comes from your request's `models` array, or from another provider that serves the same model.
See [Handle gateway errors](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/error-handling) for the full order.

A routing rule uses the first step that has usable credentials.
The gateway doesn't try later steps, except an `ngrok` step after a **Bring your own API key** step.

To attach several provider keys and control the order they're tried, see [Multi-key failover](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/key-selection-failover).

## Timeouts and token limits

Configure account-level limits in [Account Settings](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/account-settings).

| Setting | Default | Description |
| - | - | - |
| Per-request timeout | 15m | Max time for a single upstream attempt |
| Total timeout | 30m | Max time including all failover attempts |
| Max input tokens | none | Reject requests exceeding estimated input tokens |
| Max output tokens | none | Cap completion length |

For streaming responses, the per-request timeout applies only until the first byte.
After that, the stream runs until the total timeout, as long as the provider keeps sending data at least every 30 seconds.
See [Streaming responses](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/account-settings#streaming-responses).

Request bodies are limited to 32 MiB.

# Migrate from Portkey to the ngrok AI Gateway
Source: https://ngrok.com/docs/ai-gateway/migrate/portkey

Move your apps from Portkey to the ngrok AI Gateway by mapping provider keys, API keys, configs, and guardrails, then changing a few lines of client code.

If your apps call models through Portkey, you're deciding whether to follow it into Palo Alto Networks' Prisma AIRS or move your traffic somewhere else.
Palo Alto bought Portkey in May 2026.
The Prisma AIRS edition runs from Strata Cloud Manager and bills in Palo Alto flex credits, while the original Portkey product is still sold with no published end date.

The [ngrok AI Gateway](/docs/ai-gateway/overview) is a hosted gateway at `gateway.ngrok.ai` that accepts OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini API requests, so your apps keep the SDKs they use today.
ngrok hosts and upgrades it, and its price is public: a processing fee of \$0.05 per million tokens, paid from [credits](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/credits).
Pay for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and other supported models with those credits, or bring your own provider key for any built-in provider.
For agent traffic, [Firewall](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/firewall) checks each tool call a model returns and blocks risky ones before your agent runs them.

> [!NOTE]
>
> The ngrok AI Gateway doesn't yet have a built-in Vertex AI provider, an MCP gateway, response caching, per-key budgets, or PII redaction.
> It reaches Claude on Amazon Bedrock through the Anthropic and AWS SDKs, but not through OpenAI Chat Completions.
> If your apps depend on those Portkey features, read [the list of features without an equivalent yet](#features-without-an-equivalent-yet) before you decide.

This guide moves an app that calls models through Portkey to the ngrok AI Gateway.
You recreate your Portkey setup in app.ngrok.ai, run both gateways side by side, then cut over.

Most of the work is on the gateway side.
Client code usually changes in three places: the base URL, the API key, and the `model` string.

## What you'll need

* Your Portkey account, with an Admin API key or Workspace API key that can read configs, providers, guardrails, and API keys.
* An ngrok.ai account at [app.ngrok.ai](https://app.ngrok.ai) with [credits](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/credits).
* An [AI Gateway API key](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/access-keys#credentials-overview), if you want to script the setup instead of using the dashboard.
* The source code of the apps you're moving.

## 1. Inventory your Portkey setup

Portkey splits its setup between your code and its dashboard.
A default config attached to an API key can route every request without any trace of it in your code, so check both places.

### Search your code

Search your repositories for the strings that tie them to Portkey:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
rg -n --hidden \
  -e 'portkey' -e 'PORTKEY_' -e 'x-portkey-' \
  -e 'createHeaders' -e 'with_options\(' \
  -e 'virtual_key' -e 'virtualKey' \
  -e '"@[a-z0-9-]+/'
```

Each match tells you what to change:

| Match | What to change |
| - | - |
| `api.portkey.ai`, `aigw.portkey.ai`, or `PORTKEY_GATEWAY_URL` | The base URL |
| `portkey_ai` or `portkey-ai` imports, `Portkey(`, and `createHeaders` | Portkey SDK calls, which become plain OpenAI or Anthropic SDK calls |
| `x-portkey-*` headers | See [Map Portkey headers](#map-portkey-headers) |
| `@slug/model` strings and `virtual_key` values | The providers each app calls, which become provider keys and `provider:model` names |
| Checks for HTTP `246` or `446` | Error handling that reads Portkey guardrail results |

### Export your Portkey objects

Save the objects that hold your routing and credentials with the [Portkey Admin API](https://docs.portkey.ai/docs/api-reference/admin-api/introduction).
Run this once for each Portkey workspace, with an API key for that workspace:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
for resource in configs integrations providers guardrails api-keys; do
  curl -s "https://api.portkey.ai/v1/$resource" \
    -H "x-portkey-api-key: $PORTKEY_API_KEY" \
    > "portkey-$resource.json"
done
```

Each file maps to something you create in ngrok.ai:

| Portkey objects | What they become in ngrok.ai |
| - | - |
| Integrations and AI Providers (formerly virtual keys), in `portkey-integrations.json` and `portkey-providers.json` | [Provider keys](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys) |
| API keys, with their default config, budget, and rate limit, in `portkey-api-keys.json` | [Access keys](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/access-keys) and [access key configurations](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations) |
| Configs (`pc-…`), in `portkey-configs.json` | [Virtual models](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/virtual-models) |
| Guardrails (`pg-…`), in `portkey-guardrails.json` | [Firewall policies](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/firewall), in part |

In `portkey-api-keys.json`, check each key's `defaults.config_id`.
A key with a default config routes every request through that config, even when the app's code never mentions it.

If you manage Portkey with its Terraform provider, your state file already holds all of these.

## 2. Add your provider keys

Each Portkey AI Provider, such as `@openai-prod`, holds one provider credential.
Add each credential as a provider key in ngrok.ai, on the [**Providers**](https://app.ngrok.ai/providers) page or with the API:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
curl -X POST https://api.ngrok.ai/provider-keys \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "providerId": "openai",
    "name": "openai-prod",
    "value": "<OPENAI_API_KEY>"
  }'
```

Name each key after its Portkey slug so you can match them up later.

You don't need a provider key for every provider.
For OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, and [other providers that support it](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/model-catalog#billing-and-provider-credentials), skip the provider key and [pay with credits](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/pay-with-credits).

If you used several Portkey providers for the same upstream, such as two OpenAI keys for more rate-limit headroom, add both keys.
You order them in the next step.

### Amazon Bedrock

In Portkey, each Bedrock provider covers one AWS region, such as `@bedrock-us-east-1` and `@bedrock-us-west-2`.
In ngrok.ai, each Bedrock provider key covers one region, so add one key for each region you use.

ngrok.ai authenticates to Bedrock with a Bedrock API key.
If your Portkey Bedrock providers use IAM access keys or an assumed role, generate a long-term Bedrock API key in each AWS account first, as described in [Amazon Bedrock](/docs/ai-gateway/providers/bedrock#setup).
Bedrock always uses your own key; you can't pay for it with credits.

A key you add in the dashboard uses `us-east-1`.
To add a key for another region, set `aws.region` with the API:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
curl -X POST https://api.ngrok.ai/provider-keys \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "providerId": "bedrock",
    "name": "bedrock-us-west-2",
    "value": "<BEDROCK_API_KEY>",
    "aws": { "region": "us-west-2" }
  }'
```

A `us.` model ID from Portkey, such as `us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`, works with a key in any region, because the key's region decides where the request goes.
When the model doesn't run in that region, the gateway uses the inference profile for the region's geography.
A key in `eu-west-1` keeps the request in the EU.
See [Regions](/docs/ai-gateway/providers/bedrock#regions).

### Providers that aren't built in

Connect any OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible endpoint as a [custom provider](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/custom-providers).
For Azure OpenAI, follow [the Azure OpenAI guide](/docs/ai-gateway/custom-providers/azure-openai), with one custom provider per deployment or region.
Vertex AI isn't a built-in provider yet; see [Features without an equivalent yet](#features-without-an-equivalent-yet).

## 3. Recreate your API keys

In Portkey, a workspace groups API keys, providers, and configs for one team.
ngrok.ai has no workspace layer.
Give each team or app its own access key, and use an access key configuration to control what that key can call.

1. On [**Keys**](https://app.ngrok.ai/keys) → **Configurations**, create one configuration for each Portkey workspace or API key that had its own provider access.
2. Under **Access**, allow only the providers and models that team used.
3. Under **Routing**, add a rule for each provider:
   choose **Bring your own API key** and attach the provider keys from the previous step in the order to try them, or choose **ngrok** to pay with credits.
4. Create one access key for each Portkey API key you're replacing, and assign its configuration.

The same configuration through the API:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
curl -X POST https://api.ngrok.ai/access-key-configurations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "search-team",
    "access": {
      "providers": { "allow": ["openai", "anthropic"] }
    },
    "router": {
      "rules": [
        {
          "provider": "openai",
          "steps": [
            {
              "type": "user",
              "keySelectionStrategy": "ordered",
              "keys": [{ "id": "<PRIMARY_PROVIDER_KEY_ID>" }, { "id": "<BACKUP_PROVIDER_KEY_ID>" }]
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

When the first OpenAI key hits a rate limit or an auth error, the gateway tries the second.
See [Multi-key failover](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/key-selection-failover).

Put your regional Bedrock keys in one `bedrock` rule the same way, in the order to try their regions.
A rate limit in one region moves the request to the next region's key.
A server error or timeout doesn't: it skips your other Bedrock keys and moves to the next model.
If a Portkey config fails over between Bedrock regions during an outage, list a model on another provider after the Bedrock model in a virtual model, as in [Try Amazon Bedrock before Anthropic](/docs/ai-gateway/providers/bedrock#try-amazon-bedrock-before-anthropic).

app.ngrok.ai shows each access key token once, when you create it.
Store each token, which starts with `ng-`, where the app reads its Portkey key today.

## 4. Turn fallback configs into virtual models

A Portkey config with `"mode": "fallback"` becomes a [virtual model](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/virtual-models): a name your apps send as `model`, which stands for an ordered list of models.

This Portkey config tries OpenAI, then Anthropic:

```json Portkey config theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "strategy": { "mode": "fallback", "on_status_codes": [429, 500, 503] },
  "targets": [
    { "override_params": { "model": "@openai-prod/gpt-5.1" } },
    { "override_params": { "model": "@anthropic-prod/claude-sonnet-4-6" } }
  ]
}
```

Create the equivalent virtual model:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
curl -X POST https://api.ngrok.ai/virtual-models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "chat-default",
    "models": ["openai:gpt-5.1", "anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6"]
  }'
```

Apps then send `"model": "chat-default"`.
To change the models later, edit the virtual model; apps don't change.

Some config fields work differently:

| Portkey config | In ngrok.ai |
| - | - |
| `on_status_codes` and `retry` | The gateway fails over on rate limits, auth errors, server errors, timeouts, and connection failures, and returns other 4xx errors right away. You can't change that list or the number of attempts. See [what triggers failover](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/error-handling). |
| A default config on an API key that overrides `model` | Apps that send a model like `gpt-4o` need a new `model` value, because a virtual model can't share a name with a model your account can call. |
| `loadbalance` and `conditional` strategies | The gateway doesn't split traffic by weight or route on metadata. Pick the order you want most requests to use, or give each route its own virtual model. |
| Per-request configs in `x-portkey-config` | Put the fallback list in the request body's [`models` array](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/configure-fallback-models). |

## 5. Recreate guardrails with Firewall

[Firewall](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/firewall) checks what an app sends to a model and each tool call the model returns.
It covers some of what Portkey guardrails do:

| Portkey guardrail | Firewall equivalent |
| - | - |
| Regex match on input | Regex rule on request messages |
| Prompt injection or custom LLM check on input | Decision rule on request messages, written in plain language |
| Allow or deny tools in the request | Tool names rule on tool definitions |
| Checks on MCP tool calls | Tool names or regex rule on tool calls, such as `mcp__github__delete_*` |
| PII detection and redaction, output text checks, partner guardrails | None yet |

Attach a policy to the access key configuration for each team, or apply it to every key as your baseline.
Start in dry run mode to see what it would block on real traffic.
See [Guard agent tool calls with Firewall](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/firewall-policies).

Blocks look different to your app.
Portkey returns HTTP `446` when a guardrail denies a request.
Firewall returns HTTP `200` with an assistant message that explains the block and a `safeguard_results` field, so the model or agent can continue.
Update any error handling that checks for `246` or `446`.

## 6. Change your client code

Your apps keep their OpenAI or Anthropic SDK.
Change the base URL, the key, and the `model` string, and remove Portkey headers.

### OpenAI SDK with a Portkey key

```python Before theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://api.portkey.ai/v1",
    api_key=os.environ["PORTKEY_API_KEY"],
)

client.chat.completions.create(
    model="@openai-prod/gpt-5.1",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
)
```

```python After theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1",
    api_key=os.environ["NGROK_AI_ACCESS_KEY"],
)

client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai:gpt-5.1",  # or a virtual model, such as "chat-default"
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
)
```

### OpenAI SDK with createHeaders

Apps that pass Portkey settings through `createHeaders` send a provider key or a placeholder as `api_key`.
Replace it with your access key and drop the headers.

```typescript Before theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
import OpenAI from "openai";
import { PORTKEY_GATEWAY_URL, createHeaders } from "portkey-ai";

const client = new OpenAI({
  apiKey: "unused",
  baseURL: PORTKEY_GATEWAY_URL,
  defaultHeaders: createHeaders({
    apiKey: process.env.PORTKEY_API_KEY,
    virtualKey: "openai-prod",
    config: "pc-chat-default",
  }),
});
```

```typescript After theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
import OpenAI from "openai";

const client = new OpenAI({
  apiKey: process.env.NGROK_AI_ACCESS_KEY,
  baseURL: "https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1",
});
```

The routing that `virtualKey` and `config` did now lives in the access key's configuration and in the virtual model your app sends as `model`.

### Portkey SDK

Replace `Portkey` with the OpenAI client.
`Portkey` accepts the same calls as the OpenAI SDK, so `client.chat.completions.create(...)` calls don't change.

```python Before theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
import os
from portkey_ai import Portkey

client = Portkey(
    api_key=os.environ["PORTKEY_API_KEY"],
    config="pc-chat-default",
)
```

```python After theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1",
    api_key=os.environ["NGROK_AI_ACCESS_KEY"],
)
```

Calls that only exist in the Portkey SDK, such as `portkey.prompts.completions.create` and `portkey.feedback`, have no equivalent.

### Anthropic SDK

```python Before theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
client = anthropic.Anthropic(
```

```python After theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
import os

client = anthropic.Anthropic(
```

The Google Gen AI SDK follows the same pattern; see [Google Gen AI SDK](/docs/ai-gateway/sdks/google).

### Models on Amazon Bedrock

Portkey translates OpenAI Chat Completions requests for any Bedrock model.
The ngrok AI Gateway doesn't translate them for Claude or most other Bedrock models yet, so apps that reach Bedrock through the OpenAI SDK switch SDKs as well as base URLs:

| Bedrock models | Call them through ngrok.ai with |
| - | - |
| Claude Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.5, and Opus 4.6 | The Anthropic SDK and a model such as `bedrock:anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`, or the AWS SDK's InvokeModel and the Bedrock model ID |
| Gemma 4 | The OpenAI SDK, in Chat Completions or Responses, and a model such as `bedrock:google/gemma-4-31b-it` |
| Every other Bedrock model in the catalog | The AWS SDK's Converse and the Bedrock model ID, such as `openai.gpt-oss-20b-1:0` |

This example moves an app's calls to Claude Haiku 4.5 on Bedrock from the OpenAI SDK to the Anthropic SDK:

```python Before theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://api.portkey.ai/v1",
    api_key=os.environ["PORTKEY_API_KEY"],
)

client.chat.completions.create(
    model="@bedrock-us-east-1/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0",
    max_tokens=1024,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
)
```

```python After theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
import os
import anthropic

client = anthropic.Anthropic(
    base_url="https://gateway.ngrok.ai",
    api_key=os.environ["NGROK_AI_ACCESS_KEY"],
)

client.messages.create(
    model="bedrock:anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5",
    max_tokens=1024,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
)
```

The `bedrock:` prefix keeps the request on Bedrock.
Without it, `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` goes to Anthropic first.
To try Bedrock first and fall back to Anthropic, list both in a virtual model; see [Try Amazon Bedrock before Anthropic](/docs/ai-gateway/providers/bedrock#try-amazon-bedrock-before-anthropic).

For the AWS SDK, point the client's `endpoint_url` at `https://gateway.ngrok.ai` and set `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` to your ngrok.ai access key, the token that starts with `ng-`.
See [Native Bedrock requests](/docs/ai-gateway/providers/bedrock#native-bedrock-requests).

### Map model names

| Portkey `model` | ngrok.ai `model` |
| - | - |
| `@openai-prod/gpt-5.1` | `openai:gpt-5.1`, or `gpt-5.1` to let the gateway pick any provider that serves it |
| `@anthropic-prod/claude-sonnet-4-6` | `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6` |
| `@bedrock-us-east-1/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0` | `bedrock:anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`, sent with the Anthropic SDK |
| `@my-azure/gpt-4o` | `my-azure:gpt-4o`, where `my-azure` is your custom provider ID |
| `gpt-4o` routed by a config | The virtual model that replaced the config |

The gateway picks the provider key from the access key's configuration, not from the model string.
See [Choose a model](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/model-selection-strategies).

## 7. Run both gateways and cut over

Before you move an app, send one request with its new access key and read the headers:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
curl -i https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $NGROK_AI_ACCESS_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "chat-default",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
  }'
```

```http theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
HTTP/2 200
ngrok-aig-request-id: rq_2abcDEF456
ngrok-aig-attempts: 1
ngrok-aig-model: gpt-5.1
```

`ngrok-aig-model` names the model that answered, the first one in `chat-default` here, and `ngrok-aig-attempts` counts the upstream attempts the gateway made.
An error names what blocked the request, such as a provider the key's configuration doesn't allow; see [Error codes](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/error-codes).

Then move traffic over:

1. Point one app, or one environment of it, at ngrok.ai and leave the rest on Portkey.
2. Check each response's `Ngrok-AIG-Model` header to confirm the model you expect answered, and `Ngrok-AIG-Removed-Params` for request fields a provider didn't accept.
3. Compare cost and token counts on the [**Activity**](https://app.ngrok.ai/activity) page, or with the [Usage API](/docs/ai-gateway/observability), against your Portkey logs.
4. Move the remaining apps.
5. Revoke the Portkey API keys once their traffic stops.

Until you revoke those keys, moving an app back to Portkey means restoring its old base URL, key, and `model` values.

Log each response's `Ngrok-AIG-Request-Id` in your app.
It's how you look up a request later; see [Why a request failed over](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/why-a-request-failed-over).

## Map Portkey headers

ngrok.ai doesn't read `x-portkey-*` headers.
Remove them, or replace them as follows:

| Portkey header | In ngrok.ai |
| - | - |
| `x-portkey-api-key` | Send your access key as `Authorization: Bearer`, or as `x-api-key` with the Anthropic SDK |
| `x-portkey-provider`, `x-portkey-virtual-key` | The access key's configuration, plus `provider:model` in the request |
| `x-portkey-config` | A virtual model, or the `models` array in the request body |
| `x-portkey-trace-id`, `x-portkey-span-*` | None. The gateway assigns each request an ID and returns it in the `Ngrok-AIG-Request-Id` response header; log it next to your own trace ID |
| `x-portkey-metadata` | None. With [request capture](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/account-settings#request-capture) on, the request details panel shows the headers you sent |
| `x-portkey-cache-*` | None. See [Features without an equivalent yet](#features-without-an-equivalent-yet) |
| `x-portkey-request-timeout` | Account-wide timeouts in [Account Settings](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/account-settings) |
| `x-portkey-forward-headers` | None |

## Features without an equivalent yet

| Portkey feature | What to do meanwhile |
| - | - |
| Claude and most other Bedrock models through Chat Completions | Call Claude with the Anthropic SDK and other Bedrock models with the AWS SDK. See [Models on Amazon Bedrock](#models-on-amazon-bedrock). |
| Bedrock models outside the catalog, and `global.` inference profiles | Use a model from the [Amazon Bedrock catalog](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/model-catalog#amazon-bedrock), with a regional ID such as `us.` or `eu.`. |
| Bedrock failover to another region on server errors and timeouts | Rate limits still move to the next region's key. For outages, list a model on another provider after the Bedrock model in a virtual model. |
| Vertex AI provider | Call Gemini models through the built-in [Google provider](/docs/ai-gateway/providers/google), and keep Model Garden routes on Portkey for now. |
| MCP gateway and MCP registry | Keep MCP traffic where it is. To block specific MCP tools in model traffic, use a Firewall tool names rule. |
| Simple and semantic caching | Cache in your app. |
| Per-key budgets and rate limits | Use account-wide [token limits](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/account-settings#token-limits) and track spend per key with the [Usage API](/docs/ai-gateway/observability), grouped by `accessKey`. |
| PII redaction and partner guardrails | Redact in your app before sending. |
| Weighted load balancing and conditional routing | Use an ordered virtual model, or a separate access key per route. |
| Workspaces and in-app roles | Use an access key and configuration per team. Dashboard sign-in supports [SSO](/docs/iam/sso). |
| Prompt templates | Keep prompts in your code. |
| Realtime and batch APIs | Call the provider directly. |
| OpenTelemetry or log export | ngrok.ai has no push export. Read usage events with the [Usage API](/docs/ai-gateway/observability). |
| Terraform provider | Script setup with the [AI Gateway API](/docs/ai-gateway/api-reference/overview) and its [OpenAPI spec](https://api.ngrok.ai/openapi.yaml). |

# AI Gateway Observability Overview
Source: https://ngrok.com/docs/ai-gateway/observability/index

Track AI Gateway usage with the Usage API, and look up any single request by its ID in app.ngrok.ai to see what happened to it.

Monitor AI Gateway usage from [app.ngrok.ai](https://app.ngrok.ai) and the AI Gateway API.

> [card] [Usage](/docs/ai-gateway/observability/index#usage-api)
>
> Query usage events and aggregated overview via the AI Gateway API

> [card] [Debugging](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/debugging)
>
> Troubleshoot failed requests and error codes

> [card] [Error Codes](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/error-codes)
>
> Reference for gateway error responses

## Identify a request

Every gateway response carries `Ngrok-AIG-Request-Id`, plus headers such as `Ngrok-AIG-Attempts`, `Ngrok-AIG-Model`, `Ngrok-AIG-Rejected-Models`, and `Ngrok-AIG-Removed-Params` that describe how the request was served.
Record the request ID in your application logs so you can tie a client-side failure to gateway usage data later.
See [Response headers](/docs/ai-gateway/how-it-works#response-headers).

## Usage API

Query usage with the AI Gateway API:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
curl "https://api.ngrok.ai/usage/overview?startTime=2026-10-01T00:00:00Z&groupBy=accessKey" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY"
```

The overview returns daily cost, request, and error series for the window.
`startTime` is required.
Group by `provider` (the default) or `accessKey`.

[List individual usage events](/docs/ai-gateway/api-reference/usage/list) to see one record per upstream attempt.
Each event reports the provider, model, status code, token counts, and a per-attempt cost breakdown.
Attempts of the same client request share a `requestId`.
When an attempt's model came from a [virtual model](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/virtual-models), `virtualModel` holds the virtual model's name as it was when the request ran.

By default the list returns only each request's terminal attempt.
Pass `includeRetries=true` to see the retries the gateway made along the way.

> [!NOTE]
>
> When a provider reports no usage of its own, `usageEstimated` is `true` and the provider-reported token fields are all zero.
> Read `inputTokensEstimate` and `outputTokensEstimate` on those attempts instead.

## Look up one request

To see every attempt the gateway made for one request, pass its `Ngrok-AIG-Request-Id` to [`GET /usage/requests/{requestId}`](/docs/ai-gateway/api-reference/usage/request-attempts).
See [Why a request failed over](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/why-a-request-failed-over).

## Inspect a request in app.ngrok.ai

The [Activity](https://app.ngrok.ai/activity) page lists your gateway requests, newest first, with each request's outcome, model, access key, tokens, and cost.
Select a row to open **Request details**, a panel that shows what your app sent, what came back, and every attempt the gateway made along the way.
You can also open it from **Recent attempts** on the Overview page, or from **View in Activity** under an answer in the [playground](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/playground).

The top of the panel shows the HTTP status, the request ID, and a summary of the request: the API it used, the model that served it, the access key, latency, tokens, and cost.
Hover over the latency, token, or cost value for a breakdown.
Use the arrows next to the title to step through the requests in the list.
Each request and tab has its own URL, so you can share a link with someone on your account.

| Tab | What it shows |
| - | - |
| **Conversation** | The messages, tool calls, and tool results in the request, followed by the model's reply. Embeddings requests show **Embeddings** instead, and [System One](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/decisions-and-system-one) requests show **Evaluation**. |
| **Request** | The headers and body your app sent to the gateway. |
| **Response** | The headers and body the gateway returned to your app. For a streamed response, switch between **Overview** (the reconstructed output and stream milestones), **Events**, and **Raw**. |
| **Attempts** | Each attempt the gateway sent to a provider, in order, with its provider, model, outcome, timing, tokens, cost, and credential. Select an attempt to see the request the gateway sent the provider and the provider's response. |

![Request details panel on the Conversation tab, showing the HTTP status, request ID, a summary with surface, model, access key, latency, tokens, and cost, and a captured tool-calling conversation](https://mintcdn.com/ngrok/NtlJmMH9rvSW0IRo/ai-gateway/observability/img/request-details-conversation.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=NtlJmMH9rvSW0IRo\&q=85\&s=40501471fe04ef341da901e6259336e4)

The **Attempts** tab shows where time went.
Each attempt's latency breaks down into time in the gateway, time upstream, time to first token, and time spent thinking, and the attempts add up to the total request duration.
**Credential** shows **Managed by ngrok** when the attempt [paid with credits](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/pay-with-credits), or the name of your [provider key](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys).

![Attempts tab of the request details panel, showing a request that failed over from an HTTP 401 and an HTTP 429 to a third attempt that served the response, with the selected attempt's model, latency, tokens, cost, credential, and delivery](https://mintcdn.com/ngrok/NtlJmMH9rvSW0IRo/ai-gateway/observability/img/request-details-attempts.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=NtlJmMH9rvSW0IRo\&q=85\&s=473fd395fb0151bdf130e559d780568a)

### What the panel needs

The summary and the **Attempts** tab work for every request.
Headers and bodies appear only for requests made while [request capture](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/account-settings#request-capture) was on.
Capture is off by default.
Without it, the **Conversation**, **Request**, and **Response** tabs show **No content was captured** with a link to turn capture on for future requests.

### Limits

* **Retention**: captured headers and bodies are kept for 30 days.
  Request metadata, including attempts, timing, tokens, and cost, is kept for 90 days, so older requests still show their attempts after their bodies expire.
* **Size**: each captured body stores up to 4 MB, and each set of headers up to 16 KiB.
  The panel warns you when content past the limit is unavailable.
* **Redaction**: credential headers such as `Authorization`, `x-api-key`, `x-goog-api-key`, and `Cookie` are redacted and show as **Redacted**.
  On the **Request** tab, `Authorization` shows the name and ID of the access key that made the request instead.
  Bodies, including prompts and completions, are stored as sent.
* **Rejected requests**: a request the gateway rejects before it calls a provider, for example because your credit balance is empty or the access key is invalid, has no attempts, so it doesn't appear in the Activity list.
* **Not in the API**: captured headers and bodies are available in app.ngrok.ai and through the [ngrok MCP server](/docs/mcp-server/ai-gateway), not through the AI Gateway API.
  To read attempts from code, use [`GET /usage/requests/{requestId}`](/docs/ai-gateway/api-reference/usage/request-attempts).

**Have feedback?** Email [niji@ngrok.ai](mailto:niji@ngrok.ai) with observability requests.


# AI Gateway Overview
Source: https://ngrok.com/docs/ai-gateway/overview

Control which AI models your apps can call, fail over between providers automatically, and pay with credits or your own provider keys.

The ngrok AI Gateway ([ngrok.ai](https://ngrok.ai)) enables your applications to call both hosted AI providers and local models through a single endpoint. Control who has access, decide what they can call, and choose whether requests use credits, your provider keys, or a model you run yourself.

[ngrok's AI Gateway: Route to local LLMs without a VPN](https://www.youtube.com/embed/VC7vrSsSCpg)

## Why use the AI Gateway?

> [card] Start without provider accounts
>
> Use OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, xAI, and other built-in providers with an access key and credits. No provider signup required.

> [card] Route to Self-Hosted Models
>
> Route to local models like Ollama or vLLM alongside cloud providers with [a model you run yourself](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/use-a-model-you-run-yourself).

> [card] Automatic Failover
>
> If one provider or key fails, ngrok.ai automatically tries the next model or key.

> [card] Compatible With Popular SDKs
>
> Works with official and third-party SDKs. Point the base URL at `gateway.ngrok.ai` and use your access key.

## Quick example

Sign up at [app.ngrok.ai](https://app.ngrok.ai) and point your SDK at the gateway with your [access key](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/access-keys):

```python Python (OpenAI) highlight={4-5} theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1",
    api_key="ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx"  # Your access key
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-4o",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]
)
```


You don't need to sign up for OpenAI or bring your own OpenAI key to make this request. Your ngrok.ai credits will cover any provider costs.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Every request consumes [credits](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/credits).
> No subscription plan required to get started.
> See [Credits](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/credits) for more details and when you might need a ngrok subscription for features like team members or internal endpoints.

On each request, the AI Gateway:

1. Receives your request with your access key at `gateway.ngrok.ai`
2. Validates the key and loads your account configuration
3. Selects which model and provider to use
4. Forwards the request using a key ngrok.ai supplies (paid with credits) or your provider keys
5. Retries with the next key or model on failure
6. Returns the response

## What can you do?

| Use Case | Description |
| - | - |
| **Use without provider accounts** | Get started with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and [other providers](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/model-catalog#billing-and-provider-credentials) using an access key and [credits](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/credits) |
| **Per-key routing** | [Access key configurations](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations) scope providers, models, and credentials |
| **Multi-model failover** | List multiple models in a request; the gateway tries each in order |
| **Multi-key failover** | Attach multiple provider keys in a configuration routing rule |
| **Self-hosted models** | Route to Ollama, vLLM, or other servers with [a model you run yourself](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/use-a-model-you-run-yourself) |

# Use Anthropic with the AI Gateway
Source: https://ngrok.com/docs/ai-gateway/providers/anthropic

Send Claude requests through ngrok.ai, pin them to Anthropic with explicit provider routing, and upload files to reuse in later requests.

This guide walks through using [Anthropic](https://anthropic.com) Claude models with the AI Gateway.
Anthropic is a **built-in provider** you can pay for with credits, so you can use Claude models without an Anthropic account of your own, or bring your own key.

## Pay with credits (no Anthropic account)

You can use Claude models without your own Anthropic account.
ngrok.ai supplies the Anthropic credentials and bills the model cost to your credits.

### 1. Create an access key and add credits

Follow the [quickstart](/docs/ai-gateway/quickstart) to create an [access key](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/access-keys) and purchase [credits](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/credits) in [app.ngrok.ai](https://app.ngrok.ai).

### 2. Send requests

Point your SDK at the gateway with your access key:

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
import anthropic

client = anthropic.Anthropic(
    base_url="https://gateway.ngrok.ai",
    api_key="ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx",  # Access key
)

message = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-sonnet-4-6",
    max_tokens=1024,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]
)
```

```bash cURL theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
curl https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1/messages \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-api-key: ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx" \
  -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \
  -d '{"model": "claude-sonnet-4-6", "max_tokens": 1024, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]}'
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> The gateway supports both the Anthropic Messages API (`/v1/messages`) and OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions.

## Bring your own Anthropic key

Want requests billed to your own Anthropic account instead of through credits?
Store your Anthropic key once—the gateway attaches it for you on every request.

### 1. Create an access key

Follow the [quickstart](/docs/ai-gateway/quickstart) to create an [access key](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/access-keys) in [app.ngrok.ai](https://app.ngrok.ai) if you don't have one yet.

### 2. Add your Anthropic key

[Add a provider key](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys#add-a-provider-key) for Anthropic.
ngrok stores it encrypted, so it never has to live in your application or get shared around—and you can reuse it across as many access keys as you need.

### 3. Route to it with a configuration

[Create an access key configuration](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations#create-a-configuration) with an Anthropic routing rule set to **Bring your own API key**, then assign it to your access key.

### 4. Keep sending your access key

Your code doesn't change.
Send the same access key as before—the gateway swaps in your Anthropic key before the request leaves for Anthropic.

## Explicit provider routing

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
message = client.messages.create(
    model="anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6",
    max_tokens=1024,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]
)
```

## Available models

Browse the [model catalog](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/model-catalog#anthropic) for the full list of Claude models you can call through the gateway.

## Parameters the gateway removes

The gateway removes these fields before it sends a request to Anthropic, and lists them in the `Ngrok-AIG-Removed-Params` [response header](/docs/ai-gateway/how-it-works#response-headers):

* `speed` on every Claude model.
  Fast mode isn't available through the gateway, so a request with `"speed": "fast"` runs and bills at standard speed.
* `temperature`, `top_p`, and `top_k` on the models that reject them: the Claude Fable models, Claude Opus 4.7 and later, Claude Sonnet 5 and later, and Claude Haiku 5.5.
* `reasoning_effort` on Chat Completions requests to every Claude model.
  To set the effort level, send an Anthropic Messages request to `/v1/messages` with `output_config`, which the gateway forwards.

## Fable 5.2

Claude Fable 5.2 (`claude-fable-5-2`) has a 1M-token context window, up to 128K output tokens, and always uses adaptive thinking.
It takes text, image, and file input.
Effort is the main control for this model, so call it with the Messages API.
The gateway removes `reasoning_effort` from Chat Completions requests.

Anthropic returns a `400` error for some Claude Fable 5.2 requests that Claude Fable 5.1 accepts, and the gateway passes the error through.
Anthropic rejects a request that:

* Forces tool use with `tool_choice`.
* Sets `thinking` to `enabled` or `disabled`.
* Uses the `computer_20251124` tool instead of `computer_toolset_20260801`.
* Edits the system prompt, the tools, or an earlier message, and then sends back a Claude Fable 5.2 thinking block.

## Files

Anthropic also supports the [Files API](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/files) for uploading documents and images once and referencing them by ID.

# Use Amazon Bedrock with the AI Gateway
Source: https://ngrok.com/docs/ai-gateway/providers/bedrock

Learn how to call models on Amazon Bedrock through the ngrok AI Gateway with a Bedrock API key from your own AWS account.

[Amazon Bedrock](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/) runs models from Anthropic, Amazon, and open-weight labs in your AWS account.
The gateway accepts these APIs for Bedrock models:

* Anthropic Messages: send requests to `/v1/messages`.
  They reach Claude Haiku 4.5, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Opus 4.5, and Claude Opus 4.6 through InvokeModel, streaming included.
* Bedrock InvokeModel: send requests to `/model/<MODEL_ID>/invoke`, or to `/model/<MODEL_ID>/invoke-with-response-stream` for a stream.
* Bedrock Converse: send requests to `/model/<MODEL_ID>/converse`, or to `/model/<MODEL_ID>/converse-stream` for a stream.
* OpenAI Chat Completions and Responses: send requests to `/v1/chat/completions` or `/v1/responses`.
  They reach [Gemma 4](#gemma-4).

Chat Completions, Responses, Messages, generateContent, and Converse requests also reach the models that serve another of those formats, through [translation](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/use-any-model-with-any-sdk).
InvokeModel requests reach only the Claude models.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Even though Amazon Bedrock is a **built-in provider**, it still requires you to **bring your own key** because you can't pay for it with credits at this time.

## Setup

### 1. Create an access key

Follow the [quickstart](/docs/ai-gateway/quickstart) to create an access key in [app.ngrok.ai](https://app.ngrok.ai).

### 2. Turn on model access

In commercial AWS regions, AWS turns on access to most models the first time your account calls them.
For a model sold through AWS Marketplace, that first call starts a Marketplace subscription, which can take up to 15 minutes.
The identity that makes the call needs `aws-marketplace:Subscribe`, `aws-marketplace:Unsubscribe`, and `aws-marketplace:ViewSubscriptions`.
The GPT OSS models and the Amazon, MiniMax, Mistral, Moonshot AI, Qwen, and Z.ai models don't need a subscription.

Before you call a Claude model, complete the Anthropic First Time Use (FTU) form.
AWS requires it for Anthropic models earlier than Claude Opus 4.7, which covers every Claude model on this page.
Open the Anthropic model in **Model catalog** in the [Amazon Bedrock console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/) to find it.
You submit the form once per AWS account, or once in your AWS organization's management account.
See [Access Amazon Bedrock foundation models](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-access.html).

### 3. Create a Bedrock API key

In the [Amazon Bedrock console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/), open **API keys** and choose the **Long-term API keys** tab.
Click **Generate long-term API keys**, choose a time in **API key expiration**, and click **Generate**.
AWS shows the key only once, so copy it now.

Use a long-term key.
A short-term key expires with your console session, after 12 hours at most, and works only in the region that made it.

AWS attaches the `AmazonBedrockLimitedAccess` managed policy to the IAM user behind the key.
That policy already has the permissions the gateway needs.
AWS recommends API keys for exploration and short-term credentials for production.
See [Generate Amazon Bedrock API keys](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/api-keys-generate.html).

### 4. Add the key to ngrok

[Add a provider key](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys#add-a-provider-key) for Amazon Bedrock.
A key you add in the dashboard uses the `us-east-1` region.
To use another region, add the key with the [Provider Keys API](/docs/ai-gateway/api-reference/provider-keys/create) and set `aws.region`:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
curl -X POST https://api.ngrok.ai/provider-keys \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"providerId": "bedrock", "name": "Bedrock eu-west-1", "value": "<BEDROCK_API_KEY>", "aws": {"region": "eu-west-1"}}'
```

The API refuses a region where Bedrock doesn't run.
See [Regions](#regions) for how the region picks where requests go.

### 5. Create a configuration

[Create an access key configuration](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations#create-a-configuration) with a `bedrock` routing rule and allow Amazon Bedrock in the access scope.

### 6. Assign and send requests

Assign the configuration to your access key and send requests with your access key:

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
import anthropic

client = anthropic.Anthropic(
    base_url="https://gateway.ngrok.ai",
    api_key="ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx",  # Access key
)

message = client.messages.create(
    model="bedrock:anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5",
    max_tokens=1024,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]
)
```

```bash cURL theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
curl https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1/messages \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-api-key: ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx" \
  -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \
  -d '{"model": "bedrock:anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5", "max_tokens": 1024, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]}'
```

The `bedrock:` prefix keeps the request on Amazon Bedrock.
A bare `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` goes to Anthropic first.

## Scope down the key's IAM policy

The default `AmazonBedrockLimitedAccess` policy covers every call the gateway makes.
If you replace it with a narrower policy, the key's IAM user needs at least these permissions:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": "bedrock:CallWithBearerToken",
      "Resource": "*"
    },
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "bedrock:InvokeModel",
        "bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream"
      ],
      "Resource": [
        "arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/*",
        "arn:aws:bedrock:*:<ACCOUNT_ID>:inference-profile/*"
      ]
    },
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "bedrock-mantle:CallWithBearerToken",
        "bedrock-mantle:CreateInference"
      ],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```

`bedrock:CallWithBearerToken` lets the key call Bedrock as a bearer token.
Converse requests use the same two invoke permissions as InvokeModel requests.
An inference profile can run a request in any region of its geography, so the policy covers every region.
The `bedrock-mantle` statement covers Gemma 4, which runs on the bedrock-mantle endpoint.
To accept only long-term keys, add a condition on `bedrock:BearerTokenType` with the value `LONG_TERM`.
A deny on `bedrock:CallWithBearerToken` alone doesn't block API keys on bedrock-mantle.
To block them there too, also deny `bedrock-mantle:CallWithBearerToken`.
See [Revoke Amazon Bedrock API keys](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/api-keys-revoke.html).
See [Actions defined by Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/service-authorization/latest/reference/list_bedrock.html).

## Regions

Each Bedrock key sends requests to one AWS region.
A key with no region uses `us-east-1`.

The key's region picks the AWS endpoint and the model ID the gateway sends.
The endpoint is `bedrock-runtime.<REGION>.amazonaws.com`, or `bedrock-mantle.<REGION>.api.aws` for Gemma 4.
The gateway sends the model's in-region ID when the model runs in that region, and the inference profile for the region's geography otherwise.
The key's region wins over the `us.` in a model ID.
For example, a key in `eu-west-1` sends a request for `us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0` through the `eu.` inference profile.
A model ID with a different geography prefix, such as `eu.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`, uses only keys in that geography.

Gemma 4 runs in-region only, with no inference profile.
Keys in `us-east-1`, `us-east-2`, `us-west-2`, and `eu-central-1` serve it.
GLM-4.7, GLM-5, Ministral 3B, and Qwen3 Coder 30B A3B Instruct serve `us-east-1` keys only.
The gateway doesn't support `global.` model IDs.

When none of your keys is in a region that serves the model, the gateway returns a `400` error with `ERR_NGROK_AI_GATEWAY_MODEL_REGION_UNSUPPORTED`:

```text theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
No Bedrock key region serves model '<MODEL_ID>'. Key regions: <REGIONS>. Add a Bedrock key in a region that serves the model.
```

## Native Bedrock requests

Point an AWS SDK at `https://gateway.ngrok.ai` and send your ngrok access key as the bearer token.
The AWS SDKs read the bearer token from the `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` environment variable.
When `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` is set, boto3 sends the bearer token even if your shell also sets `AWS_PROFILE`.
The gateway returns errors in the Bedrock error format.
Name the model by its Bedrock model ID, such as `us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`.

Send an InvokeModel request to a Claude model:

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
import json

import boto3

# export AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK=ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx
client = boto3.client(
    "bedrock-runtime",
    region_name="us-east-1",  # the SDK needs a region; your ngrok key's region decides where the request goes
    endpoint_url="https://gateway.ngrok.ai",
)

response = client.invoke_model(
    modelId="us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0",
    body=json.dumps({
        "anthropic_version": "bedrock-2023-05-31",
        "max_tokens": 1024,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}],
    }),
)
print(json.loads(response["body"].read()))
```

```bash cURL theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
curl https://gateway.ngrok.ai/model/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0/invoke \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"anthropic_version": "bedrock-2023-05-31", "max_tokens": 1024, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]}'
```

### Stream responses

Send stream requests to `/model/<MODEL_ID>/converse-stream` or `/model/<MODEL_ID>/invoke-with-response-stream`.
The gateway returns the stream as AWS event stream frames, which the AWS SDKs read.

```python Converse theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
import boto3

# export AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK=ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx
client = boto3.client(
    "bedrock-runtime",
    region_name="us-east-1",  # the SDK needs a region; your ngrok key's region decides where the request goes
    endpoint_url="https://gateway.ngrok.ai",
)

response = client.converse_stream(
    modelId="openai.gpt-oss-20b-1:0",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": [{"text": "Hello!"}]}],
)

for event in response["stream"]:
    if "contentBlockDelta" in event:
        print(event["contentBlockDelta"]["delta"].get("text", ""), end="")
```

```python InvokeModel theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
import json

import boto3

# export AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK=ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx
client = boto3.client(
    "bedrock-runtime",
    region_name="us-east-1",  # the SDK needs a region; your ngrok key's region decides where the request goes
    endpoint_url="https://gateway.ngrok.ai",
)

response = client.invoke_model_with_response_stream(
    modelId="us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0",
    body=json.dumps({
        "anthropic_version": "bedrock-2023-05-31",
        "max_tokens": 1024,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}],
    }),
)

for event in response["body"]:
    chunk = json.loads(event["chunk"]["bytes"])
    if chunk["type"] == "content_block_delta":
        print(chunk["delta"].get("text", ""), end="")
```

## Gemma 4

Amazon Bedrock serves Gemma 4 through its OpenAI-compatible API.
Send Chat Completions or Responses requests with `bedrock:google/gemma-4-31b-it` or `bedrock:google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it`:

```bash Chat Completions theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
curl https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "bedrock:google/gemma-4-31b-it", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]}'
```

```bash Responses theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
curl https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "bedrock:google/gemma-4-31b-it", "input": "Hello!"}'
```

Google and LLM API also serve Gemma 4, so the `bedrock:` prefix keeps the request on Amazon Bedrock.

Bedrock keeps Responses output by default.
The gateway sends `store: false`, so Bedrock doesn't keep it.
The gateway removes `store` and `previous_response_id` from a Responses request to Gemma 4 and lists them in the `Ngrok-AIG-Removed-Params` [response header](/docs/ai-gateway/how-it-works#response-headers), so a request can't continue an earlier response on Bedrock.

## Try Amazon Bedrock before Anthropic

A bare Claude model ID, such as `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`, goes to Anthropic first.
The `bedrock:` prefix pins a request to Amazon Bedrock, with no fallback to another provider.

To try Amazon Bedrock first and fall back to Anthropic, create a [virtual model](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/virtual-models) that lists both:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
curl -X POST https://api.ngrok.ai/virtual-models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "claude-haiku-bedrock-first",
    "models": [
      "bedrock:anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5",
      "anthropic:anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5"
    ]
  }'
```

Send `claude-haiku-bedrock-first` as the model in a Messages request.

> [!NOTE]
>
> In an access key configuration, a [model rule](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations#routing-rules) names the catalog ID with the provider prefix, such as `bedrock:anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`.
> A rule that names a Bedrock model ID, such as `us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`, doesn't match requests yet.

## Available models

See the [model catalog](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/model-catalog#amazon-bedrock).
The gateway sends Amazon Bedrock only the models in the catalog.

Each model takes these request formats:

* Claude Haiku 4.5, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Opus 4.5, and Claude Opus 4.6: Messages and Bedrock InvokeModel.
* Gemma 4 31B and Gemma 4 26B A4B: Chat Completions and Responses.
* Every other model: Bedrock Converse.
  This page calls them the Converse models.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
| - | - |
| [`ERR_NGROK_27226`](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/error-codes#err_ngrok_27226) | The API you called doesn't reach that model. Send Messages or InvokeModel requests to the Claude models, Chat Completions or Responses requests to Gemma 4, and Converse requests to the other models. See [Available models](#available-models). |
| `ERR_NGROK_AI_GATEWAY_MODEL_REGION_UNSUPPORTED` | None of your Bedrock keys is in a region that serves the model. Add a key in a region that serves it. See [Regions](#regions). |
| `403` error that names `bedrock:CallWithBearerToken` and a service control policy | A service control policy in your AWS organization denies `bedrock:CallWithBearerToken`, which blocks API keys for the Claude and Converse models. Ask your AWS administrator to allow `bedrock:CallWithBearerToken` for the account. |
| `403` `AccessDeniedException` that says the model isn't available or needs AWS Marketplace actions | [Turn on model access](#setup) for the model in that AWS account. After you submit the FTU form, the model can stay pending and keep returning this error, so wait and retry. The gateway doesn't try your other Bedrock keys, because keys in the same account get the same refusal. |

# Use Google Gemini with the AI Gateway
Source: https://ngrok.com/docs/ai-gateway/providers/google

[Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com) provides Gemini models.
The gateway supports three APIs:

The OpenAI Responses API (`/v1/responses`) doesn't reach Google models.

> [!NOTE]

To bring your own key, generate one at [aistudio.google.com](https://aistudio.google.com), then [add a provider key](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys#add-a-provider-key).

### 3. Create a configuration

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]
)
```

## Chat models

* `lfm3-1.7b` and `lfm2.5-24b-a2b` take text.
* `lfm3-vl-2b` takes text and images.
* `lfm3-audio-2b` and `lfm3-omni-2b` take audio input and can reply with audio.
  Set `modalities` and `audio` in the request to get an audio reply.

Liquid AI returns an error for `top_p`, so the gateway removes it before it sends the request and lists it in the `Ngrok-AIG-Removed-Params` [response header](/docs/ai-gateway/how-it-works#response-headers).

## Decision models

`d1`, `d1.1`, and `d1-ultra` answer typed questions instead of chatting.
Send a `POST` request to `/v1/systemone` with a `state` and a `questions` object, as described in [Typed-question APIs](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/decisions-and-system-one#typesafe-ai-requests), and name a d1 model:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
curl https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1/systemone \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx" \
  -d '{
    "model": "d1",
    "state": "Customer: My order arrived broken and I want a refund today.",
    "questions": {
      "is_urgent": {
        "type": "noul",
        "instructions": "Is this an urgent request?"
      }
    }
  }'
```

Liquid AI also accepts an `images` field on these requests and bills each image as input tokens.
The gateway forwards `model`, `state`, `questions`, and `images`, and removes any other top-level field.

See the [model catalog](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/model-catalog#liquid-ai).

# Use LLM API with the AI Gateway
Source: https://ngrok.com/docs/ai-gateway/providers/llmapi

Call models from many labs through LLM API in the ngrok AI Gateway, and see which you can pay for with credits and which need your own key.

[LLM API](https://llmapi.ai/) serves models from many labs under one API key, including Amazon Nova, Meta Llama, Mistral, Qwen, Google Gemini and Gemma, Anthropic Claude, and OpenAI GPT models.

LLM API supports Chat Completions, Responses, and Anthropic Messages requests, and the Images API for its image models.

> [!NOTE]
>
> LLM API is a **built-in provider**.
> You can pay for many of its models with credits, and the rest need your own LLM API key.
> The **Needs BYOK?** column in the [model catalog](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/model-catalog#llm-api) shows which is which.

## Setup

### 1. Create an access key and add credits

Follow the [quickstart](/docs/ai-gateway/quickstart) to create an access key and purchase [credits](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/credits) in [app.ngrok.ai](https://app.ngrok.ai).

### 2. Store your LLM API key (optional)

Skip this step to pay with credits for the models that support it.
To bring your own key, create an API key in your [LLM API](https://llmapi.ai/) account.
Then [add a provider key](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys#add-a-provider-key) and [create an access key configuration](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations#create-a-configuration) with an `llmapi` routing rule that uses it.

### 3. Send requests

Send requests with your access key:

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1",
    api_key="ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx",
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="amazon/nova-pro",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]
)
```

Many LLM API models are also served by their own labs.
Add the `llmapi:` prefix, as in `llmapi:google/gemma-4-31b-it`, to keep the request on LLM API.

## Which models work with credits

LLM API can send a request to a different upstream than the one the model names, and it bills the price of the upstream it picks.
A model works with credits only when no upstream that LLM API might pick charges more than the catalog price.
Models with long-prompt price tiers, separate cache-write prices, or image input priced apart from text need your own LLM API key.
That includes every Claude model.

## Request formats

* **Chat Completions and Responses**: Most chat models accept Chat Completions only.
  The OpenAI models, `xai/grok-4.7`, `meta/muse-wonder-1.0`, and `qwen/qwen3-coder-next` also accept Responses.
* **Messages**: LLM API serves the Anthropic Messages API for Claude models only.
* **Images**: The image models, such as `openai/gpt-image-2`, `z-ai/glm-image`, and `qwen/qwen-image-2.0`, serve the Images API at `/v1/images/generations`.
  Some of them also serve `/v1/images/edits`.

The gateway removes these fields before it sends a request to LLM API, and lists them in the `Ngrok-AIG-Removed-Params` [response header](/docs/ai-gateway/how-it-works#response-headers):

* `web_search_options` and `web_search`, because LLM API runs and bills its own web search when either is present.
* A top-level `cache_control`.
* `store` and `previous_response_id` on Responses requests, because LLM API doesn't store responses.

See the [model catalog](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/model-catalog#llm-api).

Source: https://ngrok.com/docs/ai-gateway/providers/openai

## Pay with credits (no OpenAI account)
