### 2. Send requests

Point your SDK at the gateway with your access key:

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1",
    api_key="ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx"  # Access key
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-4o",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]
)
```

```bash cURL theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
curl https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx" \
  -d '{"model": "gpt-4o", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]}'
```

## Bring your own OpenAI key

Want requests billed to your own OpenAI account instead of through credits?
Store your OpenAI key once—the gateway attaches it for you on every request.

### 1. Create an access key

Follow the [quickstart](/docs/ai-gateway/quickstart) to create an [access key](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/access-keys) in [app.ngrok.ai](https://app.ngrok.ai) if you don't have one yet.

### 2. Add your OpenAI key

[Add a provider key](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys#add-a-provider-key) for OpenAI. ngrok stores it encrypted, so it never has to live in your application or get shared around—and you can reuse it across as many access keys as you need.

### 3. Route to it with a configuration

[Create an access key configuration](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations#create-a-configuration) with an OpenAI routing rule set to **Bring your own API key**, then assign it to your access key.

### 4. Keep sending your access key

Your code doesn't change. Send the same access key as before—the gateway swaps in your OpenAI key before the request leaves for OpenAI.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Even though OpenRouter is a **built-in provider**, it still requires you to **bring your own key** because you can't pay for it with credits at this time.

## Setup

### 2. Store your OpenRouter API key

Create an account at [openrouter.ai](https://openrouter.ai) and generate an API key from your dashboard. Then [add a provider key](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys#add-a-provider-key).

### 3. Create a configuration

### 4. Assign and send requests

Assign the configuration to your access key and send requests with your access key:

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
from openai import OpenAI

    base_url="https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1",
    api_key="ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx",
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openrouter:anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]
)
```

## Model names

> [!WARNING]
>
> Always prefix OpenRouter model IDs with `openrouter:`. Without the prefix, the gateway may route to the native provider instead of OpenRouter.

OpenRouter uses a `provider/model` format for its model IDs. When calling through the ngrok AI Gateway, prefix with `openrouter:`:

| What you want | Model string to use |
| - | - |
| Anthropic Claude via OpenRouter | `openrouter:anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet` |
| Google Gemini via OpenRouter | `openrouter:google/gemini-2.0-flash-001` |
| Meta Llama via OpenRouter | `openrouter:meta-llama/llama-3.1-8b-instruct` |
| Mistral via OpenRouter | `openrouter:mistralai/mistral-7b-instruct` |

The `openrouter:` prefix tells the gateway to route to OpenRouter specifically. Without it, a slash-separated ID such as `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` resolves to the native catalog model, and the gateway sends it to the native provider first.

For the full list of models OpenRouter supports, see [openrouter.ai/models](https://openrouter.ai/models).

## Setup

### 1. Create an access key and add credits

Follow the [quickstart](/docs/ai-gateway/quickstart) to create an access key and purchase [credits](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/credits) in [app.ngrok.ai](https://app.ngrok.ai).

### 2. Store your QwenCloud API key (optional)

Skip this step to pay with credits.
To bring your own key, create an API key in your [QwenCloud](https://qwencloud.com) account.
Then [add a provider key](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys#add-a-provider-key) and [create an access key configuration](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations#create-a-configuration) with a `qwencloud` routing rule that uses it.

### 3. Send requests

Send requests with your access key:

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1",
    api_key="ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx",
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="qwencloud:qwen/qwen3.8-max",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]
)
```

For a model that other providers also serve, such as `moonshotai/kimi-k3`, add the `qwencloud:` prefix to keep the request on QwenCloud.

## Thinking and tool calls

QwenCloud's Chat Completions API differs from OpenAI's in two ways that affect requests through the gateway:

* **Thinking:** QwenCloud turns thinking on and off with its own `enable_thinking` field, and sets a token budget with `thinking_budget`.
  The gateway forwards both.
  It removes `reasoning_effort` and lists it in the `Ngrok-AIG-Removed-Params` [response header](/docs/ai-gateway/how-it-works#response-headers).
  Qwen3.8 Max thinks by default.
  Some models, such as `z-ai/glm-5.3` and `qwen/qwen3.8-2.4t-a95b`, always think, and QwenCloud rejects requests that set `enable_thinking` to `false`.
  The gateway also removes both fields for the Qwen3.5 Omni models, because QwenCloud refuses thinking on their audio requests.
* **Tool choice:** QwenCloud doesn't support `tool_choice: "required"`.
  While thinking is on, `tool_choice` accepts only `auto` or `none`, so turn thinking off to force a specific tool.
  The gateway forwards `tool_choice` as sent, so QwenCloud returns the error.

In the OpenAI Python SDK, send these fields in `extra_body`:

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="qwencloud:qwen/qwen3.8-max",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}],
    extra_body={
        "enable_thinking": True,
        "thinking_budget": 4096,
    },
)
```

See QwenCloud's [thinking](https://docs.qwencloud.com/developer-guides/text-generation/thinking) and [function calling](https://docs.qwencloud.com/developer-guides/text-generation/function-calling) guides for details.

## Available models

See the [model catalog](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/model-catalog#qwencloud).
The Qwen3.5 Omni models can also return audio.

# Use Typesafe AI with the AI Gateway
Source: https://ngrok.com/docs/ai-gateway/providers/typesafeai

Send typed questions to Typesafe AI System One models through the ngrok AI Gateway and get back typed answers with calibrated probabilities.

[Typesafe AI](https://typesafe.ai) serves System One models.
Instead of a chat conversation, a System One request sends a `state` and a set of typed `questions`. The response returns a typed answer for each question, with a calibrated probability.

Typesafe AI only supports System One requests at `https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1/systemone`. Chat Completions, Responses, and Messages requests don't reach Typesafe AI models.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Typesafe AI is a **built-in provider** you can pay for with credits, so a provider key is optional.
> Add your own Typesafe AI key to bill usage to your Typesafe AI account instead of your ngrok.ai credits.

## Setup

### 1. Create an access key and add credits

Follow the [quickstart](/docs/ai-gateway/quickstart) to create an access key and purchase [credits](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/credits) in [app.ngrok.ai](https://app.ngrok.ai).

### 2. Store your Typesafe AI API key (optional)

Skip this step to pay with credits.
To bring your own key, create an API key in your [Typesafe AI](https://typesafe.ai) account. Then [add a provider key](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys#add-a-provider-key) and [create an access key configuration](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations#create-a-configuration) with a `typesafeai` routing rule that uses it.

### 3. Send requests

Send a `POST` request to `/v1/systemone` with your access key:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
curl https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1/systemone \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx" \
  -d '{
    "model": "jev-latest",
    "state": "Customer: My order arrived broken and I want a refund today.",
    "questions": {
      "urgency": {
        "type": "score",
        "instructions": "How urgent is this message?",
        "criteria": [
          "Not urgent: no action needed.",
          "Somewhat urgent: handle within a few days.",
          "Urgent: handle today."
        ]
      }
    }
  }'
```

## Request format

A System One request body has three fields:

| Field | Description |
| - | - |
| `model` | The model ID, such as `jev-latest`. |
| `state` | The text the model evaluates. |
| `questions` | An object that maps each question ID to a typed question. It must contain at least one question. |

The gateway removes any other top-level field before it forwards the request.
System One doesn't stream, so a request with `"stream": true` returns an error.

See the [Typesafe AI API reference](https://docs.typesafe.ai) for question types and the response format.

## Available models

See the [model catalog](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/model-catalog#typesafe-ai). `jev-latest` points at the current Jev build, and `jev-preview` points at the next one.

# AI Gateway Quickstart
Source: https://ngrok.com/docs/ai-gateway/quickstart

Route your application's LLM requests through ngrok.ai so you can switch models, fail over between providers, and track usage.

This quickstart shows you how to send your first request through the ngrok AI Gateway, which gives your applications a single endpoint for models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and other providers.
You sign in to ngrok.ai, buy credits, create an access key, and use the OpenAI SDK to send a request to a GPT model.
The same access key works with every built-in provider, and you don't need an account or API key with any of them.

## Making your first request

### 1. Sign in to app.ngrok.ai

Open [app.ngrok.ai](https://app.ngrok.ai) and sign in with your ngrok account.

### 2. Purchase credits

[Top up at least \$5.00](https://app.ngrok.ai/billing).
Every request you make requires [ngrok.ai credits](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/credits).

### 3. Create your access key

Open [Access Keys](https://app.ngrok.ai/keys) and create a new key.
Copy the key right away—it's shown only once—and store it somewhere safe.
It looks like `ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx`.

### 4. Make your first request

Point your OpenAI SDK at the gateway using your access key:

```js highlight={4,5} theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
import OpenAI from "openai";

const openai = new OpenAI({
  baseURL: "https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1",
  apiKey: "ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx"
});

const res = await openai.chat.completions.create({
  model: "gpt-4o",
  messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Hello, world!" }]
});
```

You don't need to sign up with OpenAI or bring your own keys for this request.
ngrok.ai handles the billing for you.

## Already have credits and an access key?

Give this to your AI coding agent to complete the SDK integration step automatically.

Complete the ngrok AI Gateway SDK integration (I've already signed up on app.ngrok.ai, purchased credits, and have an access key):

1. Ask me for my access key (format: ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx). The gateway URL is always [https://gateway.ngrok.ai](https://gateway.ngrok.ai)
2. Install the OpenAI SDK: `npm install openai` or `pip install openai`
3. Write a script that routes OpenAI SDK requests through the gateway by setting baseURL to [https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1](https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1) and apiKey to my ng-xxxxx key
4. Send a test request with model `gpt-4o` and message "State your exact model name and provider."
5. Print and verify the response

Ask me for my access key before writing any code.

# Error Codes Reference
Source: https://ngrok.com/docs/ai-gateway/reference/error-codes

Look up any ngrok AI Gateway error code to find out what it means, and learn how to handle gateway errors in your SDK code.

These errors apply to requests sent to `https://gateway.ngrok.ai` with an [access key](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/access-keys).
Every response carries the request's ID in `Ngrok-AIG-Request-Id`, so quote that value when you contact support.
See [Response headers](/docs/ai-gateway/how-it-works#response-headers).

## Request and routing errors

The gateway rejects these before it makes any upstream attempt, so the response carries no `Ngrok-AIG-Attempts` header and the request is not billed.

### ERR_NGROK_27228

**Message**

Invalid request: `REASON`

**HTTP Status**

400 Bad Request

**Causes**

* The request body is not valid JSON
* A required field is missing for the API surface you called
* A field holds a value the surface does not accept
* No model in the request can take the request in another API format, so the gateway [skipped every model](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/use-any-model-with-any-sdk#when-the-gateway-skips-a-model)

**Solutions**

* Check the reason in the message for the offending field.
* Verify the body matches the API surface you posted to, whether Chat Completions, Responses, Messages, or the native Gemini surface.
* For a skipped model, remove the field named by the message, or pick a model that serves the API surface you posted to.

***

### ERR_NGROK_27224

**Message**

Unknown model "`MODELID`".`SUGGESTION`

**HTTP Status**

400 Bad Request

**Causes**

* The model ID is misspelled
* The model is not in the [model catalog](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/model-catalog) and no custom provider defines it

**Solutions**

* Check the suggestion in the message, which names the closest catalog match
* Look the model up in the [model catalog](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/model-catalog)
* Qualify the model with its provider, such as `openai:gpt-4o`.
  See [Choose a model](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/model-selection-strategies)

***

### ERR_NGROK_27225

**Message**

Unknown provider "`PROVIDERID`".

**HTTP Status**

400 Bad Request

**Causes**

* The provider prefix is misspelled
* The provider is a custom provider that does not exist on your account

**Solutions**

* List your providers with the [Providers API](/docs/ai-gateway/api-reference/providers/list)
* [Register the custom provider](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/custom-providers) before routing to it

***

### ERR_NGROK_27230

**Message**

"`MODEL`" is not a known model, and "`PROVIDER`" is not a recognized provider.

**HTTP Status**

400 Bad Request

**Causes**

* A provider-qualified model name whose prefix is neither a known provider nor part of a real model ID

**Solutions**

* Use `provider:model`, with the provider exactly as the [Providers API](/docs/ai-gateway/api-reference/providers/list) reports it
* Drop the prefix to let the gateway resolve the model from the catalog

***

### ERR_NGROK_27229

**Message**

Invalid model address "`ADDRESS`".

**HTTP Status**

400 Bad Request

**Causes**

* The model field is empty, or holds more separators than `provider:model` allows

**Solutions**

* Send either a bare model ID or a single `provider:model` pair

***

### ERR_NGROK_27204

**Message**

Unsupported API surface "`PATH`".

**HTTP Status**

400 Bad Request

**Causes**

* The request path is not one the gateway serves

**Solutions**

* Post to `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, `/v1/messages`, `/v1/decisions`, `/v1/systemone`, `/v1/files`, `/v1/embeddings`, `/v1/images/generations`, `/v1/images/edits`, `/v1/audio/speech`, the native Gemini path `/v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent`, or `/v1beta/interactions`
* The gateway does not serve `/v1/completions`
* Point your SDK's base URL at `https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1` rather than a full endpoint path

***

### ERR_NGROK_27226

**Message**

Provider "`PROVIDERID`" does not support API surface "`SURFACE`".

**HTTP Status**

400 Bad Request

**Causes**

* The provider has no equivalent of the surface you called, such as the Responses API on a provider that only serves Chat Completions

**Solutions**

* Call the surface the provider supports.
  See the provider's page under [Getting Started With](/docs/ai-gateway/providers/openai)
* Choose a different provider for that surface

***

### ERR_NGROK_27205

**Message**

API surface "`SURFACE`" is not implemented.

**HTTP Status**

501 Not Implemented

**Causes**

* The gateway knows this endpoint but doesn't support it yet

**Solutions**

* Use a supported endpoint such as `/v1/chat/completions`.
  See [ERR_NGROK_27204](#err_ngrok_27204) for the full list

***

### ERR_NGROK_27250

**Message**

ngrok doesn't store interactions yet, so "store" can't be true. Omit it or set it to false to send a stateless request.

**HTTP Status**

400 Bad Request

**Causes**

* An Interactions API request set `store` to `true`

**Solutions**

* Omit `store`, or set it to `false`.
  See [Google SDK](/docs/ai-gateway/sdks/google)

***

## Access policy errors

### ERR_NGROK_27231

**Message**

Provider "`PROVIDERID`" is not allowed by the access policy.

**HTTP Status**

403 Forbidden

**Causes**

* The access key's configuration does not include the provider in its access scope

**Solutions**

* Allow the provider in the key's [access key configuration](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations)
* See [Restrict providers and models](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/restrict-providers-and-models) for how scope is evaluated

***

### ERR_NGROK_27232

**Message**

Model "`MODELID`" is not allowed by the access policy.

**HTTP Status**

403 Forbidden

**Causes**

* The configuration's access scope excludes the model, even though the provider is allowed

**Solutions**

* Add the model to the access scope in the key's [access key configuration](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations)

***

## Credential and credit errors

### ERR_NGROK_27201

**Message**

Authentication failed: `REASON`

**HTTP Status**

401 Unauthorized

**Causes**

* No access key in the request
* The access key is malformed, revoked, or deleted

**Solutions**

* Send your [access key](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/access-keys) as `Authorization: Bearer ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx`, or as `x-api-key` on the Anthropic surface and `X-Goog-Api-Key` on the native Gemini surface
* Confirm the key still exists with the [Access Keys API](/docs/ai-gateway/api-reference/access-keys/list)

***

### ERR_NGROK_27202

**Message**

No keys available for provider "`PROVIDERID`".

**HTTP Status**

502 Bad Gateway

**Causes**

* The access key's configuration has no routing credentials for the requested provider
* Every provider key the configuration referenced was deleted

**Solutions**

* Add a routing rule for the provider in the key's [access key configuration](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations)
* [Attach a provider key](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys#add-a-provider-key), or [pay with credits](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/pay-with-credits) where the provider supports it

***

### ERR_NGROK_27206

**Message**

Credit check failed: `REASON`

**HTTP Status**

402 Payment Required

**Causes**

* The account's credit balance is zero or below, or billing is not set up for the account yet
* Every request needs credits, even with your own provider keys, because each one pays a small processing fee

**Solutions**

* Check your balance with the [Credits API](/docs/ai-gateway/api-reference/credits/balance)
* [Purchase credits](https://app.ngrok.ai/billing).
  Your own provider key does not bypass this check

***

### ERR_NGROK_27233

**Message**

Model "`MODELID`" is not available with an ngrok-managed key for provider "`PROVIDERID`": add your own provider key to use uncataloged models.

**HTTP Status**

400 Bad Request

**Causes**

* The model isn't in the ngrok.ai catalog, so ngrok.ai has no price for it

**Solutions**

* [Attach your own provider key](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys) for that provider
* Pick a catalog model instead.
  See the [model catalog](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/model-catalog)

***

### ERR_NGROK_27239

**Message**

ngrok can't serve "`MODELID`" on provider "`PROVIDERID`" with an ngrok-managed key right now. Add your own provider key to use it.

**HTTP Status**

503 Service Unavailable

**Causes**

* You can't pay for this model with credits on that provider right now

**Solutions**

* Retry, or fail over to another model.
  See [Configure fallback models](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/configure-fallback-models)
* [Attach your own provider key](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys) for that provider

***

### ERR_NGROK_27236

**Message**

Model "`MODELID`" is not priced for managed billing yet for provider "`PROVIDERID`"; add your own provider key to use it.

**HTTP Status**

400 Bad Request

**Causes**

* You can't pay for this model with credits on that provider yet, because ngrok.ai doesn't have a price for it

**Solutions**

* [Attach your own provider key](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys) for that provider
* Pick another model from the [model catalog](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/model-catalog)

***

### ERR_NGROK_27238

**Message**

An ngrok-managed key can't serve this request, because ngrok can't bill `FEATURE` for "`MODELID`" on provider "`PROVIDERID`". Add your own provider key to use it.

**HTTP Status**

400 Bad Request

**Causes**

* The request uses a feature, such as a hosted tool, that you can't pay for with credits on that model

**Solutions**

* Remove the feature from the request
* [Attach your own provider key](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys) for that provider

***

### ERR_NGROK_27249

**Message**

ngrok doesn't offer "`MODELID`" on provider "`PROVIDERID`" with an ngrok-managed key. Add your own provider key to use it.

**HTTP Status**

400 Bad Request

**Causes**

* The model exists in the catalog, but you can't pay for it with credits on that provider

**Solutions**

* [Attach your own provider key](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys) for that provider
* Pick a model you can pay for with credits.
  See the [model catalog](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/model-catalog#billing-and-provider-credentials)

***

### ERR_NGROK_27240

**Message**

Your account has no `FILES` for provider "`PROVIDERID`". An ngrok-managed key can only use files your account uploaded. Upload the file first, or add your own provider key.

**HTTP Status**

404 Not Found

**Causes**

* The request uses a file that wasn't uploaded from your account, so you can't pay for it with credits

**Solutions**

* [Attach your own provider key](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys) to use files stored in your provider account

***

## Upstream failures

These arrive after the gateway tries at least one provider, so `Ngrok-AIG-Attempts` tells you how many tries the gateway made.
See [Handle gateway errors](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/error-handling) for the order it tries them in.
When every model fails, or the request hits the 10-attempt cap, the gateway returns the last model's error.

### ERR_NGROK_27211

**Message**

Upstream provider rejected the API key.

**HTTP Status**

401 Unauthorized

**Causes**

* The provider key stored in ngrok is invalid, revoked, or rotated at the provider

**Solutions**

* [Rotate the provider key](/docs/ai-gateway/api-reference/provider-keys/rotate) to the current value
* Verify the key directly against the provider

***

### ERR_NGROK_27217

**Message**

Upstream provider rate limit exceeded.

**HTTP Status**

429 Too Many Requests

**Causes**

* Every credential and candidate the gateway tried was rate limited

**Solutions**

* Attach more [provider keys](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys) so the gateway has another credential to try
* Add candidates from other providers.
  See [Multi-provider failover](/docs/ai-gateway/examples/multi-provider-failover)
* Slow your request rate, or raise your quota with the provider

***

### ERR_NGROK_27207

**Message**

Upstream request timed out.

**HTTP Status**

504 Gateway Timeout

**Causes**

* A single upstream attempt exceeded the per-request timeout

**Solutions**

* Raise the per-request timeout in [Account Settings](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/account-settings)
* Shorten the prompt, or choose a faster model

***

### ERR_NGROK_3810

**Message**

Request timed out after `TIMEOUT`. Try a shorter prompt or increase your timeout.

**HTTP Status**

504 Gateway Timeout

**Causes**

* Every attempt together exceeded the total timeout
* Too many slow candidates in the failover list

**Solutions**

* Raise the total timeout in [Account Settings](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/account-settings)
* Lower the per-request timeout so a slow provider fails sooner and leaves budget for the next candidate
* Reduce the number of failover candidates

***

### ERR_NGROK_27227

**Message**

No backend available: `REASON`

**HTTP Status**

502 Bad Gateway

**Causes**

* None of the models in the request could be used, for example because the access key can't reach them
* With `ngrok/auto`, none of the models the key can reach are available for automatic selection.
  See [Automatic model selection](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/automatic-model-selection)

**Solutions**

* Confirm the configuration's routing rules cover the provider you requested
* See [Handle gateway errors](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/error-handling) for the order the gateway tries models in

***

### ERR_NGROK_27237

**Message**

Request rejected: a routing loop was detected. Double check your custom provider URLs do not cause an infinite proxy loop.

**HTTP Status**

502 Bad Gateway

**Causes**

* A custom provider's base URL points back at the AI Gateway

**Solutions**

* Point the custom provider at its real upstream.
  See [Use a model you run yourself](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/use-a-model-you-run-yourself)

***

## Limit errors

### ERR_NGROK_3811

**Message**

Input too large: `INPUTTOKENS` tokens (max `MAXALLOWED`). Shorten your prompt.

**HTTP Status**

413 Payload Too Large

**Causes**

* The prompt and context exceed the account's max input tokens
* Very long conversation history, or large embedded content in messages

**Solutions**

* Reduce the prompt length or conversation history
* Raise or clear `maxInputTokens` in [Account Settings](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/account-settings)
* Count tokens client-side before sending

***

### ERR_NGROK_AI_GATEWAY_REQUEST_BODY_TOO_LONG

**Message**

Request body is too long. Max 32 MiB.

**HTTP Status**

413 Payload Too Large

**Causes**

* The request body is larger than 32 MiB

**Solutions**

* Upload large documents and images with the [Files API](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/files) instead of sending them inline
* Reduce the conversation history or embedded content

***

## Retired setup

### ERR_NGROK_3820

**Message**

```text theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
AI Gateway has a new home at https://app.ngrok.ai. The old ai-gateway traffic
policy action has been retired. Existing credits have been migrated to
https://app.ngrok.ai. If you have any questions or issues, please reach out to
support@ngrok.com.
```

**HTTP Status**

403 Forbidden

**Causes**

* A Traffic Policy still contains the retired `ai-gateway` action

**Solutions**

* Remove the `ai-gateway` action from the endpoint's Traffic Policy
* Send LLM traffic to `https://gateway.ngrok.ai` with an [access key](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/access-keys) instead, and manage the gateway at [app.ngrok.ai](https://app.ngrok.ai)
* Credits from the retired setup were migrated automatically.
  Email [support@ngrok.com](mailto:support@ngrok.com) if your balance looks wrong

## SDK error handling

Handle ngrok errors in your SDK:

```python OpenAI Python SDK theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
from openai import OpenAI, APIError

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1",
    api_key="ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx"
)

try:
    response = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="gpt-4o",
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
    )
except APIError as e:
    print(f"Error code: {e.code}")
    print(f"Message: {e.message}")
    if "ERR_NGROK_27224" in str(e):
        print("Model not found - check model name spelling")
```

```javascript OpenAI Node.js SDK theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
import OpenAI from 'openai';

const client = new OpenAI({
  baseURL: 'https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1',
  apiKey: 'ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx',
});

try {
  const response = await client.chat.completions.create({
    model: 'gpt-4o',
    messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Hello' }],
  });
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof OpenAI.APIError) {
    console.log('Status:', error.status);
    console.log('Message:', error.message);
    if (error.message.includes('ERR_NGROK_27224')) {
      console.log('Model not found - check model name spelling');
    }
  }
}
```

# Firewall Reference
Source: https://ngrok.com/docs/ai-gateway/reference/firewall

Firewall policy fields and limits, the plugins request field, response headers, safeguard_results, and the errors Firewall returns.

This page lists the exact formats and limits for [Firewall](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/firewall).
To set up a policy, see [Guard agent tool calls with Firewall](/docs/ai-gateway/guides/firewall-policies).

## Policy fields

You manage saved policies in [app.ngrok.ai](https://app.ngrok.ai) under **Firewall**, or with the [Firewall Policies API](/docs/ai-gateway/api-reference/firewall-policies/create).
Each field shows its dashboard label first, then its name in the [`plugins` field](#the-plugins-field).
The API uses the same names, except that it spells `on_error` as `onError` and puts every rule in one `rules` list, where each rule sets its `tier` to `hardDeny`, `softDeny`, or `allow`.

| Field | Values and limits |
| - | - |
| **Name** | Required. Up to 255 characters. Saved policies only. |
| **Description** | Up to 255 characters. Saved policies only. |
| **Mode** `mode` | **Enforce** (`enforce`) or **Dry run** (`audit`). Default `enforce`. |
| **On error** `on_error` | **Block** (`block`) or **Continue** (`log`). Default `block`. |
| **Environment details** `environment` | Up to 32 facts of up to 1,000 characters each. |
| **Request rules** and **Response rules** `hard_deny`, `soft_deny`, `allow` | 1 to 48 [rules](#rule-fields) per policy. In `plugins`, each tier is its own list. |

## Rule fields

| Field | Values and limits |
| - | - |
| `id` | Required. 1 to 64 lowercase letters, digits, `_`, and `-`, unique in the policy. The dashboard sets it from the rule name. |
| **Rule name** `name` | Up to 120 characters. Defaults to the ID. |
| **Tier** | **Hard block**, **Soft block**, or **Allow**. In `plugins`, the list the rule is in sets its tier. |
| **Type** `kind` | **Regex** (`regex`), **Decision** (`decision`), or **Tool names** (`tool`). Default `decision`. |
| **Pattern** `pattern` | An [RE2](https://github.com/google/re2/wiki/Syntax) regex of up to 1,000 characters. Required for regex rules. |
| **Match** `instructions` | What a decision rule catches, in plain language, up to 8,000 characters. Required for decision rules. |
| **Min. confidence %** `threshold` | Decision rules only. A number from `0` to `1`, which the dashboard shows as a percentage. Default `0.6` for block rules and `0.7` for allow rules. |
| **Tool names** `tools` | 1 to 64 tool names of up to 128 characters, with no spaces. `*` is a wildcard. Required for tool names rules. |
| **Reads** `targets` | `messages`, `tool_results`, `tool_definitions`, or `tool_calls`. Default `tool_calls`, which can't be combined with the others. Tool names rules read `tool_calls` or `tool_definitions`. |

Each rule type takes only its own match field.
For example, a regex rule with `instructions` is rejected.

### Matching details

* **Tool names** match the whole name and are case-sensitive.
  `*` matches any characters, so `mcp__github__*` matches `mcp__github__create_issue`.
* **Regex** patterns are case-sensitive unless they start with `(?i)`.
  Against a tool call, the pattern matches the tool name, a space, and the raw JSON arguments.
  Block rules also match the arguments with JSON escapes decoded.
* **Regex** rules on request parts match all the text of each part, across every message, joined with newlines.
* In a Responses request, `instructions` and `prompt.variables` count as messages, call items as assistant turns, and `*_call_output` items as tool results.
  Tool definitions include tools that a tool search or an MCP tool list added to the conversation.
* In a Gemini request, `systemInstruction` and the `contents` parts count as messages, `functionResponse` parts as tool results, and `functionDeclarations` as tool definitions.
  Images, audio, and video have no text to read.
  Firewall can't read a PDF or other file part, so **On error** decides for rules that read the part.
* **Decision** rules on request parts read the system and developer messages plus the newest input: the latest user message and any tool results it carries.
  They read up to about 41 KB of text.
  When the text is longer, the `Ngrok-AIG-Firewall-Request` header reports a [partial read](#response-headers).

## The `plugins` field

Add a `plugins` array to a `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, `/v1/messages`, or Gemini `generateContent` request body to check that request with extra rules.
The gateway removes the field before it sends the request to the provider.

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "plugins": [{
    "id": "firewall",
    "mode": "enforce",
    "on_error": "block",
    "classifier_context": {
      "v": 1,
      "auto_mode": {
        "environment": ["Trusted repo: github.com/acme/app"],
        "hard_deny": [
          { "id": "force-push", "name": "Force push", "kind": "regex", "pattern": "git push .*--force" }
        ],
        "soft_deny": [
          { "id": "destructive", "name": "Destructive command", "instructions": "Deletes files or data, and the user didn't ask for it." }
        ],
        "allow": [
          { "id": "build-cleanup", "name": "Build cleanup", "kind": "regex", "pattern": "rm -rf \\./build/" }
        ]
      }
    }
  }]
}
```

| Field | Description |
| - | - |
| `id` | Always `firewall`. |
| `mode` | `enforce` or `audit` (Dry run). |
| `on_error` | `block` or `log` (Continue). |
| `classifier_context.v` | Always `1`. |
| `classifier_context.auto_mode` | `environment`, `hard_deny`, `soft_deny`, and `allow`, as in [Policy fields](#policy-fields). Leave out a list you don't need. |

The rules in `plugins` run on top of the saved policies that apply to the key, as described in [How policies combine](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/firewall#how-policies-combine).
A request can add up to 48 rules, and a rule can't reuse the ID of a rule in a saved policy.

The policy editor in the dashboard shows a ready-to-copy `plugins` field for the policy you're editing, under **Try it in one request**.

## What a blocked caller gets

A block returns HTTP `200`, so agents keep running and the model can react.
In Dry run, nothing is blocked, but the same results appear in the header and `safeguard_results`.

### Blocked request

When a request rule blocks a request, the gateway doesn't send it to the model.
The response holds one assistant message with this text, in the response format of the endpoint you called:

```xml theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
<ngrok_firewall_blocked_request rule="[Force push]">This request was blocked by ngrok.ai Firewall before it reached the model.</ngrok_firewall_blocked_request>
```

`rule` lists the names of the rules that blocked the request.
Each name is in brackets, with a space between names.
When Firewall couldn't check the request and **On error** is **Block**, `rule` is empty and the text says the request couldn't be checked.

### Blocked tool call

When a response rule blocks a tool call, the gateway removes the call and adds this text to the assistant message.
In a Responses request, an assistant `message` item with this text takes the call's place in `output`.
In a Gemini request, a text part with this text takes the call's place and keeps the call's `thoughtSignature`:

```xml theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
<ngrok_firewall_blocked tool="bash" rule="[Force push]">Tool call "bash" was blocked by ngrok.ai Firewall and was not executed. Do not retry it with the same arguments.</ngrok_firewall_blocked>
```

`rule` names only rules from enforced policies.
When Firewall couldn't check the call and **On error** is **Block**, `rule` is empty and the text says the call couldn't be evaluated.

If no tool calls remain, the response ends as if the model had finished:

* Chat Completions: `finish_reason` changes to `stop`.
* Messages: `stop_reason` changes from `tool_use` to `end_turn`.

### `safeguard_results`

Responses carry a top-level `safeguard_results` array when Firewall checked something.
In a streamed response, it's in the final chunk for Chat Completions, in the `message_delta` event for Messages, in the `response` object of the final event, such as `response.completed`, for Responses, and in the chunk with a `finishReason` for Gemini.

Request rules report one entry per rule:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "type": "request_rule",
  "status": {
    "type": "available",
    "rules": {
      "prompt-injection": {
        "type": "evaluated",
        "outcome": "matched",
        "explanation": "[Prompt injection]",
        "targets": ["tool_results"]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Tool call checks report one entry per tool call ID:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "type": "dangerous_tool_use",
  "status": {
    "type": "available",
    "tool_uses": {
      "call_abc123": { "type": "evaluated", "outcome": "flagged", "explanation": "[Force push]" }
    }
  }
}
```

| Field | Values |
| - | - |
| `type` (per rule or call) | `evaluated`, or `unavailable` when the check couldn't run. `unavailable` entries carry a `reason`, such as `unsupported_tool` for an [OpenAI-defined tool](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/firewall#things-to-know) whose arguments Firewall can't read. |
| `outcome` (request rules) | `matched` or `not_matched`. |
| `outcome` (tool calls) | `flagged` or `not_flagged`. |
| `explanation` | The names of the rules that matched, each in brackets, including rules from Dry run policies. |

A Gemini function call often has no ID.
Its entry then uses the call's position in the response, such as `candidates[0].parts[1]`.

A response with no tool calls carries no `dangerous_tool_use` entry.

### Response headers

| Header | Values | When present |
| - | - | - |
| `Ngrok-AIG-Firewall-Request` | `not_flagged`, `flagged; rules=<ids>`, or `unavailable`. Adds `; partial=<id>:<checked>/<total>` when a decision rule read only part of a long text. | Whenever request rules run, in both modes. |
| `Ngrok-AIG-Firewall` | `unscreened; reason=<reason>`, where the reason is `unsupported_endpoint`, `legacy_functions`, `stream_function_call_arguments`, or `unreadable_response` | When Firewall let a request or response through without checking it. |

The header lists rule IDs, while the blocked message and `safeguard_results` show rule names.
The dashboard sets each ID from the rule's name when you create the rule.

Tool call results have no header, because the gateway may already be streaming the response.
Read `safeguard_results` for them.

## Errors

| Situation | Status | Error |
| - | - | - |
| The `plugins` field is malformed or a rule is invalid | 400 | [`ERR_NGROK_27228`](/docs/ai-gateway/reference/error-codes#err_ngrok_27228). The message names the field, such as `plugins: plugins[0] is not an object`. |
| A request with `plugins` goes to an endpoint Firewall doesn't check | 400 | `ERR_NGROK_27228`: `Firewall is not available on this endpoint.` |
| An enforced policy with **On error** set to **Block** applies to the key, and the request goes to an endpoint Firewall doesn't check | 400 | `ERR_NGROK_27228`: `this access key enforces a Firewall policy with on_error block, and Firewall cannot screen this endpoint` |
| A request uses the legacy `functions` field, and an enforced response rule has **On error** set to **Block** | 400 | `ERR_NGROK_27228`: `Firewall screens tool calls, not legacy function calls. Send tools in place of functions.` |
| A streamed Gemini request sets `streamFunctionCallArguments`, and an enforced response rule has **On error** set to **Block** | 400 | `ERR_NGROK_27228`: `Firewall screens whole function calls, not streamed function call arguments. Remove streamFunctionCallArguments.` |
| Firewall can't read the tool calls in a response at all, with **Enforce** and **On error** set to **Block** | 500 | Internal Server Error with `ERR_NGROK_27209`. In a stream that has started, the gateway sends this as an error event and ends the stream. |

A single check that can't run, such as a decision model timeout, doesn't return an error.
With **Block** set, it blocks the request or tool call with the `200` responses described in [What a blocked caller gets](#what-a-blocked-caller-gets).


# Model Catalog
Source: https://ngrok.com/docs/ai-gateway/reference/model-catalog

Find the built-in providers and models ngrok.ai supports, and see how the gateway matches the model names in your requests.

ngrok.ai maintains a catalog of known providers and models.
This catalog enables automatic model resolution, routing, model validation, and rich metadata for selection strategies.

## How the catalog works

When you send a request with a model name like `gpt-4o`, the gateway automatically:

1. Resolves the model using the catalog
2. Finds every provider that serves the model, with the model author's own provider (for example, OpenAI) first, and applies the right provider credentials
3. Routes the request to the provider’s endpoint

To explicitly select a provider, use the `provider:model` format in the model string.
For example:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"css-variables","dark":"css-variables"}}
{
  "model": "openai:gpt-4o",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
}
```

## Built-in providers

The catalog includes built-in providers—public AI APIs with known models and routing metadata.
You can manage them on the [Providers page](https://app.ngrok.ai/providers).

Each provider lists its chat models first.
Speech, embedding, and music models follow in a separate table that names the API surface each model takes.
Send those requests to these gateway paths:

| API surface | Path |
| - | - |
| Embeddings | `/v1/embeddings` |
| Gemini EmbedContent | `/v1beta/models/{model}:embedContent` |
| Speech | `/v1/audio/speech` |
| Gemini GenerateContent | `/v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent` |
| Interactions | `/v1beta/interactions` |
| MiniMax T2A | `/v1/t2a_v2` |
| xAI TTS | `/v1/tts` |
| DashScope speech | `/api/v1/services/aigc/multimodal-generation/generation` for Qwen3-TTS |
| DashScope speech | `/api/v1/services/audio/tts/SpeechSynthesizer` for Qwen-Audio |

### Authentication

Send traffic using an [access key](/docs/ai-gateway/concepts/access-keys).
This key authenticates your requests to the gateway, not to the upstream provider.

### Billing and provider credentials

The AI Gateway splits billing into two parts: using the gateway and paying the model provider.

Many built-in models don’t need a provider key.
You can spot them in the tables below: if **Needs BYOK?** says “No,” you can use the model right away as long as you have credits.
The gateway takes care of authentication and charges your credits.
Availability is per model, so a provider can have some models you can pay for with credits and some you can't.

Other providers do need a key.
For those, add your provider key in app.ngrok.ai.
The provider bills you directly for model usage, and your credits cover the gateway fee.
This is often called BYOK (bring your own key).

| **Website** | [openai.com](https://openai.com/) |
| **API surfaces** | Responses, Chat Completions, Decisions, Images, Embeddings |
